title: Clinician adherence to peri-procedural warfarin bridging guidelines for patients with atrial fibrillation enrolled in an anticoagulation management service.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The 2023 AHA/ACC/HRS guidelines recommend against peri-procedural bridging of warfarin in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) based solely on CHA₂DS₂-VASc score without additional thromboembolic (TE) risk factors. At our institution, decisions regarding bridging in moderate-to-high TE risk AF patients who require anticoagulation interruption incorporate patient-specific factors. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate adherence to institutional peri-procedural guidelines and associated TE and bleeding events. METHODS: This retrospective, single-center, observational study included AF patients receiving warfarin for stroke prevention enrolled in the anticoagulation management service. Patients had moderate-to-high TE risk (CHA₂DS₂-VASc ≥5 or other TE risk factors) and underwent moderate-to-high bleeding risk procedures between August 2023 and August 2024. Major outcomes included a composite of TE events (deep vein thrombosis, pulmonary embolism, cerebrovascular accidents, or transient ischemic attack) and a composite of International Society on Thrombosis and Haemostasis (ISTH) major and clinically relevant non-major bleeding (CRNMB) events within 30 days post-procedure. Minor outcomes included individual components of the composite outcomes and adherence to the institutional guideline. RESULTS: Of the 145 procedures, bridging therapy was used in 87 (60%) and omitted in 58 (40%), with 92.4% compliance to institutional guidance. No TE events were observed. Of 21 bleeding events, one ISTH major bleed occurred in the bridging group and was attributed to the procedure, while 20 were CRNMB events. There were 15 (17.4%) CRNMB events in the bridging group and 5 (8.6%) in the non-bridging group. CONCLUSION: High adherence to institutional bridging guidelines was observed. A trend towards fewer bleeding events with no increased TE events was found in the non-bridging group in patients with moderate-to-high TE risk.

At our institution, decisions regarding bridging in moderate-to-high TE risk AF patients who require anticoagulation interruption incorporate patient-specific factors. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate adherence to institutional peri-procedural guidelines and associated TE and bleeding events.

title: Covered Stent Assisted Coil Embolisation of a Rare Splenomesenteric Artery Aneurysm - A Case Report and Literature Review.
abstract: BackgroundSplenomesenteric artery aneurysms are a rare clinical entity occurring in <1% of the population, where the splenic artery originates from the superior mesenteric artery (SMA). These aneurysms carry a high risk of rupture due to exposure to high-flow hemodynamic stress near the SMA origin.Case PresentationA 76-year-old female was incidentally diagnosed with a 1.6 cm saccular splenomesenteric aneurysm during investigation for sepsis. The patient underwent successful endovascular exclusion using a combination of a microvascular plug and coil embolisation to address the aneurysm 'front' and 'back' doors, while a covered stent was deployed in the SMA to prevent coil prolapse and preserve mesenteric perfusion. Follow-up at 3 months confirmed successful exclusion with preserved visceral flow.DiscussionDue to the rarity of this anatomical variant, documented in less than 60 cases in English literature, no standardised treatment algorithm exists. This study adds to the literature by demonstrating procedural innovation, refining management strategies and advocating for early intervention for such conditions.

title: Percutaneous joint preparation for tibiotalocalcaneal arthrodesis: a case series.
abstract: PURPOSE: Tibiotalocalcaneal (TTC) arthrodesis is a limb-salvaging procedure for end-stage ankle and hindfoot pathology but carries substantial risks of nonunion and complications. Minimally invasive approaches may reduce surgical morbidity while maintaining fusion outcomes. METHODS: This was a retrospective case series of patients who underwent TTC arthrodesis with percutaneous joint preparation between January 2020 and March 2025 at a single academic Level II trauma center. The primary outcome was radiographic or clinical fusion at final follow-up. Secondary outcomes included alignment, operative variables, complications, and functional recovery as measured by Patient Reported Outcomes Measurement Information System (PROMIS) domains. RESULTS: 2 Thirteen patients (six females) met inclusion criteria with a mean age of 74.0 years and body mass index of 27.1 kg/m. The mean time from injury to surgery in trauma patients was 6.2 days. Fibular fixation was performed in six cases (46.2%), with additional fixation necessary in select patients. Mean clinical follow-up time was 15.0 ± 4.3 months. Most patients advanced to weightbearing in supportive footwear and reported functional improvement. PROMIS Pain Interference averaged 56.8 ± 10.9, Physical Function 37.7 ± 12.2, and Global Pain 38.7 ± 28.9. Radiographs and computed tomography demonstrated moderate fusion rates in this cohort. Complications included wound issues (23.1%), hardware problems (46.2%), and one tibial shaft fracture after a fall; five patients required secondary screw removal. CONCLUSION: Percutaneous TTC arthrodesis demonstrated moderate radiographic fusion rates, functional improvement, and an acceptable complication profile for this cohort of predominantly elderly, medically complex patients.

Minimally invasive approaches may reduce surgical morbidity while maintaining fusion outcomes. METHODS: This was a retrospective case series of patients who underwent TTC arthrodesis with percutaneous joint preparation between January 2020 and March 2025 at a single academic Level II trauma center.

title: Critical-sized bone defects: essential concepts for the higher orthopaedic examination.
abstract: PURPOSE: To provide a practical review of the assessment and management of critical-sized bone defects (CSDs) for candidates preparing for higher orthopaedic examinations. METHODS: This narrative review considers definitions and classification, clinical assessment, acute management, reconstructive techniques and salvage options. RESULTS: A critical-sized bone defect (CSD) is unlikely to heal without intervention because of its size and location, although no numerical threshold defines criticality. Assessment should consider skeletal stability, infection, vascularity, soft tissues, host factors and likely function. After resuscitation, priorities include debridement, skeletal stabilisation and soft-tissue cover. Definitive bone loss should be assessed after debridement, which may require multiple operations. Reconstruction may be single-stage or staged. Options include bone grafting or acute shortening in selected cases, bone transport, the induced-membrane technique and vascularised bone transfer. Patient-specific implants show promise, but long-term evidence is limited. Planning should involve an orthoplastic team, with microbiology input if infection is suspected. Amputation should be considered if reconstruction is unlikely to yield a functional limb. CONCLUSION: Successful management requires infection control, stable fixation and reliable soft-tissue cover. The reconstructive approach should reflect the defect and the patient's circumstances, balancing likely functional benefit against the burden of treatment.

title: Renal trauma: an overview of current management.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Following liver and splenic injury, the kidney is the third most common abdominal organ to be injured and is frequently associated with injuries to other organs. Management has shifted to conservative treatment, which is associated with increased organ preservation. The urologist, as part of a multi-disciplinary team, must review the clinical status, associated organ injuries and imaging findings to decide how to intervene. OBJECTIVES: To provide an overview of the current management strategies and guidelines for renal trauma. METHODS: A comprehensive literature review on renal trauma was conducted using the PubMed and Google Scholar databases, with a focus on recent findings and the latest guideline recommendations. RESULTS: Sound clinical decision-making is required when selecting a management strategy. Selective non-operative management has become the new standard in haemodynamically stable patients. Advances in imaging, endoscopy and endovascular treatment have shifted the management of renal trauma towards minimally invasive approaches. Urinary diversion is reserved for cases with complications due to urinary extravasation. Renorrhaphy must be performed in suitable cases. CONCLUSION: Selective non-operative management has been embraced as the new standard in renal trauma, with a resultant decreased nephrectomy rate. The urologist must take all factors into account to identify those that may lead to adverse outcomes and to intervene promptly.

title: The START-SIAPAV-PAD Registry - Rationale, study design, and baseline characteristics of an ongoing Italian multicentre registry.
abstract: Background: Patients and methods: Results Conclusions: Peripheral artery disease (PAD) is associated with a high burden of cardiovascular and limb events, yet guideline-directed medical therapy remains suboptimal. The START-SIAPAV-PAD registry was designed to describe characteristics, management and clinical history of patients with PAD in Italy. Baseline characteristics and treatment are reported.START-SIAPAV-PAD is a prospective, multicentre, observational registry enrolling consecutive adults with PAD managed at 20 Italian Vascular centres, starting in February 2023. Standardised electronic case-report forms collect demographics, risk factors, comorbidities, haemodynamic parameters, vascular anatomy, therapies. Follow-up is planned for a minimum of 3 years. PAD severity is classified according to the Leriche-Fontaine scale, and risk-factor targets follow the 2024 ESC guidelines.: The present analysis includes 517 patients (72.0% male; median age 71 years) with a high prevalence of hypertension (79.2%), dyslipidaemia (85.0%), diabetes (36.9%), smoking (96.1% current or former) and chronic kidney disease (21.2%). Nearly half reported a walking distance <200 m, 77.5% had a resting ankle-brachial index ≤.80, and 17.2% presented with Leriche-Fontaine stage IV. Femoropopliteal disease was most frequent (69.8%), with multilevel involvement in 43.4%. Previous revascularisation was common, major amputation was rare. LDL cholesterol target (<55mg dL) was achieved in 27.9% of patients despite lipid-lowering therapy in 82.1%. Dual pathway inhibition, advanced lipid-lowering therapies, supervised exercise and structured smoking-cessation programmes were insufficiently adopted.In a population with advanced PAD and multiple risk factors we observed a substantial gap between guideline recommendations and real-world practice. Longitudinal follow-up will assess outcomes and opportunities to improve PAD management.

Baseline characteristics and treatment are reported.START-SIAPAV-PAD is a prospective, multicentre, observational registry enrolling consecutive adults with PAD managed at 20 Italian Vascular centres, starting in February 2023.

title: A conserved motif in Pch2 regulates its localization and meiotic function in Saccharomyces cerevisiae.
abstract: The Saccharomyces cerevisiae Pch2 protein is a conserved meiotic AAA+ ATPase whose activity must be tightly regulated to ensure proper chromosome dynamics during meiotic prophase I. Its function relies on remodeling the HORMA-domain protein Hop1, promoting conformational transitions that are essential for chromosome axis organization, checkpoint signaling, and recombination control. Here, we identify threonine 428 (T428), located within a conserved threonine-glutamine (TQ) motif, as a residue critical for Pch2 localization and function. We found that, in zip1Δ cells, the meiotic recombination checkpoint response is partially or completely abolished in the pch2-T428A and pch2-T428D mutants, respectively. Both mutations alter Pch2 subcellular localization, leading to its increased nuclear accumulation; however, forced nuclear exclusion of Pch2-T428A, but not Pch2-T428D, restores the zip1Δ meiotic block, indicating an additional effect of the T428D substitution on checkpoint function beyond subcellular distribution. Analysis in synapsis-proficient strains reveals that this residue also plays a critical role in coordinating Hop1 chromosomal enrichment with Mek1 activation along the synaptonemal complex. In contrast to pch2Δ or the ATPase-defective pch2-E399Q mutant, introduction of a negative charge at position 428 uncouples Hop1 accumulation from its phosphorylation, preventing Mek1 activation despite robust Hop1 association with meiotic chromosomes. These findings support emerging models in which Pch2 regulates Hop1 to control not only its chromosomal abundance, but also the maintenance of sufficient levels of Hop1 in a phosphorylation-competent conformation, thereby ensuring proper checkpoint signaling and faithful meiotic progression.

title: Venous Thromboembolism in Acute Necrotizing Pancreatitis Is Associated With Worse Outcomes, With Subtype-Specific Patterns: A Nationwide Analysis, 2016-2022.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) complicates acute necrotizing pancreatitis (ANP), but outcomes across extra-splanchnic deep vein thrombosis (DVT), portal vein thrombosis (PVT), and splenic vein thrombosis (SVT) remain poorly defined. We evaluated national trends and in-hospital outcomes in ANP with versus without VTE and across VTE subtypes. METHODS: Using the National Inpatient Sample (2016-2022), adults hospitalized with principal ANP were identified. Secondary diagnosis codes captured VTE subtypes. Primary analyses compared mortality and major complications in ANP with versus without VTE; secondary analyses compared outcomes by subtype. RESULTS: Among 110,225 ANP hospitalizations, 12.25% had VTE. ANP with VTE had higher in-hospital mortality (aOR 1.89, P<0.001), longer length of stay (adjusted mean difference 10.7 d, P<0.001), and higher hospitalization charges (adjusted mean difference $151,685, P<0.001). VTE was associated with higher rates of mesenteric ischemia, gastric varices, upper GI bleeding, AKI, sepsis, shock, respiratory failure, ARDS, vasopressor use, mechanical ventilation, blood transfusion, and ICU admissions. On subtype analysis, DVT (aOR 2.39, P<0.001) and PVT (aOR 1.45, P=0.001) were associated with higher mortality; SVT was not significantly associated with mortality, though the analysis was limited by few events. PVT was most strongly associated with mesenteric ischemia (aOR 8.28, P<0.001), whereas gastric varices were most associated with SVT (aOR 11.37, P<0.001) and PVT (aOR 3.73, P<0.001). CONCLUSIONS: VTE in ANP was associated with higher in-hospital mortality, systemic complications, and resource utilization, with substantial heterogeneity across subtypes. DVT-associated ANP showed higher rates of systemic complications, whereas PVT and SVT showed distinct territory-specific vascular-complication patterns. Prospective studies should evaluate phenotype-specific anticoagulation strategies.

METHODS: Using the National Inpatient Sample (2016-2022), adults hospitalized with principal ANP were identified.

title: Post Hoc Association Between Intramuscular Injection Site and Ulcer Healing in Patients with Chronic Limb-Threatening Ischemia Treated with Recombinant Human Hepatocyte Growth Factor Naked Plasmid: AAnalysis of the HOPE CLTI-2 Trial.
abstract: post hoc p p p p p p p p This study was based on the multicenter, double-blind, randomized phase III HOPE CLTI-2 trial. An exploratoryanalysis was performed to investigate the association between intramuscular injection site and ulcer healing outcomes in patients with chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) treated with recombinant human hepatocyte growth factor (rh-HGF), and to explore factors associated with ulcer healing. The analysis included 108 patients with CLTI treated with rh-HGF, comprising 184 ischemic lower-limb ulcers. Patients were classified according to injection site into a single-segment group, with injections limited to the calf muscles, and a multi-segment group, with injections administered to both the thigh and calf muscles. Outcomes included ulcer healing rate, time to ulcer healing, ankle-brachial index (ABI), Rutherford category, Wound, Ischemia, and foot Infection (WIfI) classification, and adverse clinical events. At the study endpoint, the unadjusted ulcer healing rate was significantly higher in the single-segment group than in the multi-segment group (75.0% vs. 57.1%,= 0.014), and the observed time to ulcer healing was shorter (153.00 [91.00-184.00] days vs. 181.00 [94.00-191.00] days,= 0.022). No significant between-group differences were observed in changes in ABI (= 0.290) or in WIfI classification (= 0.407). However, the distribution of Rutherford categories at study endpoint favored the single-segment group (= 0.016). In the multivariable logistic regression analysis, baseline ulcer area (odds ratio [OR]: 0.684, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.519-0.901,= 0.007) and male sex (OR: 3.924, 95% CI: 1.164-13.232,= 0.028) were independently associated with ulcer healing. Although the unadjusted comparisons favored the single-segment group, injection site was not independently associated with ulcer healing after multivariable adjustment (OR: 1.560, 95% CI: 0.703-3.460,= 0.269). Therefore, these findings should be considered hypothesis-generating. Whether a more anatomically targeted rh-HGF injection strategy under a fixed-dose regimen can improve ulcer healing requires evaluation in prospectively designed studies.

title: Cause-Specific Endovascular Thrombectomy Time Windows in Basilar Artery Occlusion: ATTENTION Trial Post Hoc Analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) outperforms best medical treatment (BMT) for basilar artery occlusion (BAO), but the influence of stroke cause on the time sensitivity of EVT remains unclear. We hypothesized nonatherosclerotic BAO would require earlier EVT, whereas atherosclerotic BAO-with chronic stenosis and more robust collaterals-would retain EVT benefit in extended windows. We conducted a post hoc 3-way interaction analysis of the ATTENTION trial (Trial of Endovascular Treatment of Acute Basilar Artery Occlusion) to explore cause-specific EVT time patterns. METHODS: Using randomized ATTENTION trial data (36 Chinese centers, 2021-2022), patients were stratified by onset-to-puncture time (<6 versus ≥6 hours) and TOAST (Trial of ORG 10172 in Acute Stroke Treatment) cause (atherosclerotic: large-artery atherosclerosis; nonatherosclerotic: cardioembolism/undetermined/other causes). The primary outcome was 90-day favorable functional outcome (modified Rankin Scale score 0-3), with relative risk as the primary estimand; the 3-way interaction was tested via joint Wald test. A weighted 1-hour interval odds ratio trend analysis served as an exploratory tool, with multivariable regression adjusting for confounders. RESULTS: P P P P P P Among 340 patients (226 EVT+BMT, 114 BMT), for onset-to-puncture time <6 hours, patients without atherosclerosis with EVT achieved a significantly higher favorable outcome rate (46.7% versus 20.4%; relative risk, 2.29 [95% CI, 1.25-4.18];=0.007); patients with atherosclerosis showed numerical outcome benefit (40.4% versus 26.1%,=0.259). For onset-to-puncture time ≥6 hours, numerical benefit of patients with atherosclerosis increased from 14.3% to 30.6% (56.9% versus 26.3%;=0.199), accompanied by ordinal modified Rankin Scale score improvement (common odds ratio, 3.30 [95% CI, 1.13-9.62];=0.029) and National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale score reduction; patients without atherosclerosis' benefit decreased from 26.3% to 17.8% with loss of significance (39.5% versus 21.7%,=0.341). The treatment time×cause interaction was not significant (=0.662). The weighted 1-hour interval odds ratio trend analysis identified a provisional 5.3-hour reference point in patients without atherosclerosis. CONCLUSIONS: Compared with nonatherosclerotic BAO, atherosclerotic BAO appears less time-sensitive, potentially retaining EVT responsiveness over longer windows. These findings are hypothesis-generating and require prospective validation. REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT04751708.

title: Comparison of DOAC Versus VKA for Cerebral Venous Thrombosis: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Cerebral venous thrombosis is an uncommon cause of stroke that primarily affects young adults. Several clinical trials and observational studies have compared vitamin K antagonists (VKAs) with direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) for treating cerebral venous thrombosis, but the small sample sizes limit the ability to draw firm conclusions. METHODS: We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials and observational studies comparing DOACs with VKAs for the treatment of cerebral venous thrombosis. Studies published between January 2007 and July 2025 were included. Prespecified subgroup analyses were conducted by study design, DOAC class (anti-factor Xa inhibitors versus direct thrombin inhibitors), and VKA. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane Risk-of-Bias Tool 2 for randomized trials and the Risk of Bias in Nonrandomized Studies of Interventions for observational studies. Pooled risk ratios (RRs) with 95% CIs were calculated using random-effects models. RESULTS: P Fourteen studies (8 randomized clinical trials [RCTs] and 6 observational studies) were included. Among 3698 patients, 1669 (45.1%) received DOACs and 2029 (54.9%) received VKAs. Rates of recurrent venous thromboembolism (10.24% versus 10.99%), major bleeding (4.26% versus 6.18%), clinically relevant nonmajor bleeding (2.63% versus 1.66%), good functional outcomes (95.09% versus 89.25%), and mortality (3.37% versus 3.30%) were similar in DOACs and VKAs. Recurrent venous thromboembolism was similar between DOACs and VKAs in RCTs (RR, 1.06 [95% CI, 0.35-3.24]) and in the overall pooled analysis of all studies (RR, 0.92 [95% CI, 0.55-1.53]). Major bleeding did not differ between DOACs and VKAs in RCTs (RR, 0.73 [95% CI, 0.24-2.22]) or in the overall analysis (RR, 0.74 [95% CI, 0.44-1.25];=0.26). Clinically relevant nonmajor bleeding was also comparable in RCTs (RR, 1.06 [95% CI, 0.25-4.48]) and overall (RR, 1.22 [95% CI, 0.38-3.86]). Good functional outcomes (modified Rankin Scale score of 0-2) were similar between DOACs and VKAs in RCTs (RR, 1.00 [95% CI, 0.84-1.19]) and in the combined analysis of all studies (RR, 1.02 [95% CI, 0.93-1.11]). Mortality was similar between DOACs and VKAs in RCTs (RR, 1.15 [95% CI, 0.28-4.68]) and in the pooled analysis. When direct thrombin inhibitors were compared with factor Xa inhibitors, there were no significant differences in outcomes. CONCLUSIONS: DOACs demonstrated comparable efficacy and safety to VKAs in the treatment of cerebral venous thrombosis. These findings support the use of DOACs as a reasonable alternative.

Several clinical trials and observational studies have compared vitamin K antagonists (VKAs) with direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) for treating cerebral venous thrombosis, but the small sample sizes limit the ability to draw firm conclusions. METHODS: We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials and observational studies comparing DOACs with VKAs for the treatment of cerebral venous thrombosis.

title: Multidisciplinary Collaboration in the Performance of Aortic Surgery: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association.
abstract: Intraoperative management of a patient undergoing cardiac surgery requires continuous and independent interventions by multiple healthcare professionals, including surgeons, anesthesiologists, and perfusionists, among others. Although each clinician performs tasks based on their training and accepted techniques, guidelines, and protocols, an action by one member of the team can have immediate consequences for other team members. Aortic surgery adds a level of complexity, with the need for interventions such as single-lung ventilation, systemic cooling (and subsequent rewarming), and myocardial, cerebral, and visceral protection. Much has been made of the utility of the multidisciplinary team. This scientific statement is intended to approach the patient undergoing aortic surgery from 3 different viewpoints: that of the surgeon, the anesthesiologist, and the perfusionist. This scientific statement is not intended to provide an exhaustive summary of approaches to aortic surgery but rather to illustrate the specific concerns that each member of the team may have.

title: Vascular access management after kidney transplantation position paper on behalf of the Vascular Access Society and the European Kidney Transplant Association.
abstract: There is no consensus on whether to ligate or preserve uncomplicated vascular access (VA) after kidney transplantation (KT), as International Guidelines do not address this issue. Enhanced survival rates of kidney grafts may elevate the risk of cardiac morbidity and mortality due to prolonged exposure to the hemodynamic effects of arterio-venous fistulas (AVF). Although VA ligation reduces left ventricle (LV) mass, its impact on cardiovascular (CV) morbidity or mortality is unclear. High-flow VAs can complicate KT patients, and immunosuppressive medication may increase these complications. Despite preserving VA for future hemodialysis (HD) use, central catheters are used in nearly two-thirds of patients. Detecting transplant patients who can undergo AVF ligation and reconstruction when returning to HD allows for flexible decision-making with a multidisciplinary approach, personally tailored to patients at their discretion. Therefore, an algorithm involving Doppler ultrasound and cardiac evaluation is advisable.

title: GLP-1 Receptor Agonist Use before Total Knee Arthroplasty is Associated with Lower Postoperative MI, DVT, and VTE Rates.
abstract: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) are increasingly prescribed for glycemic control and weight management, but their association with postoperative thrombotic events after total knee arthroplasty (TKA) remains unclear. We performed a retrospective cohort study using de-identified data from the TriNetX United States Collaborative Network, including adults who underwent primary TKA between December 1, 2006, and June 1, 2025. Patients with prior myocardial infarction (MI), deep vein thrombosis (DVT), venous thromboembolism (VTE), or pulmonary embolism (PE) were excluded. Exposure was defined as a prescription for a GLP-1 RA within 1 year and 1 day before surgery. A 1:1 propensity score match was performed on demographics, relevant comorbidities, and medications, yielding 11,765 patients in each cohort. Outcomes were postoperative MI, DVT, VTE, and PE. Compared with matched controls, patients prescribed GLP-1 RAs had a significantly lower risk of MI (25/11,246 vs. 47/11,171; risk ratio [RR] 0.528; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.325-0.858). GLP-1 RAs use was also associated with a reduced risk of DVT (74/11,319 vs. 103/11,308; RR 0.718; 95% CI, 0.533-0.966) and VTE (133/11,040 vs. 172/11,027; RR 0.772; 95% CI, 0.617-0.967). In contrast, no statistically significant difference was observed in the incidence of PE between groups (49/11,352 vs. 58/11,382; RR 0.847; 95% CI, 0.580-1.238). Overall, preoperative GLP-1 RA use was associated with a significantly lower postoperative risk of MI, DVT, and VTE following TKA in this large, nationally representative cohort.

title: Co-occurrence of aortic dissection and polycystic kidney disease: a case report.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Aortic dissection is a rare and often fatal condition which arises when there is aortic wall weakening. Multiple risk factors could lead to this condition, including hypertension, atherosclerosis, connective tissue diseases such as Marfan's, Ehlers-Danlos and Loeys Dietz syndromes, as well as smoking, cocaine usage, bicuspid aortic valve, pregnancy and trauma. Polycystic kidney disease (PKD) is a rare condition characterized by the development of multiple renal cysts, which is caused by genetic abnormalities leading to autosomal dominant or autosomal recessive inheritance. However, the presentation of both pathologies simultaneously is rare and has been infrequently reported. CASE PRESENTATION: We report a death attributed to the co-occurrence of both conditions, involving a 19-year-old Caucasian male with no known past medical history, who collapsed during sexual intercourse. Post-mortem examination revealed hemopericardium with an aortic dissection, which was associated with PKD. The heart and the great vessels were sent to the author's place of practice for a detailed cardiovascular pathology examination. CONCLUSION: This case is a reminder to all forensic and clinical pathologists that an extremely uncommon manifestation can occur; therefore, a meticulous approach should always be adopted before corroborating a cause of death, especially in young individuals. The relationship between both conditions in this case remains uncertain; however, PKD may represent an associated finding and possibly a predisposing factor rather than a direct causal mechanism. The co-occurrence of both pathologies raises the likelihood of an underlying predisposition to vascular pathology and may have implications for the screening and clinical evaluation of surviving blood relatives.

Multiple risk factors could lead to this condition, including hypertension, atherosclerosis, connective tissue diseases such as Marfan's, Ehlers-Danlos and Loeys Dietz syndromes, as well as smoking, cocaine usage, bicuspid aortic valve, pregnancy and trauma. title: Efficacy and Safety of Endovascular Treatment for HIR- and Collateral-Screened Ultra-Long Window Anterior Circulation LVO: A Prospective Cohort Study.
abstract: This study investigated the clinical value of combined hypoperfusion intensity ratio (HIR) and collateral evaluation for patient selection and prognostic assessment in endovascular therapy (EVT) among anterior circulation large vessel occlusion (LVO) patients within the 6-24 h extended time window. This prospective cohort analysis enrolled 152 LVO patients treated with EVT between January 2022 and June 2024. HIR was defined as the volume ratio of Tmax >10 s to Tmax >6 s hypoperfusion. Collateral status was assessed using the Tan scale, with scores ≥3 classified as favorable. According to the HIR cutoff (≤0.4) and collateral status, patients were divided into four subgroups: Group A (dual favorable), Group B (favorable HIR/poor collaterals), Group C (poor HIR/favorable collaterals), and Group D (dual unfavorable). All participants received standard EVT and adjunct medical therapy for comparative outcome analysis. Groups A (n = 42), B (n = 38), C (n = 35), and D (n = 37) differed significantly in baseline stroke severity and perfusion parameters, with Group D presenting larger ischemic cores, extensive hypoperfusion, and higher NIHSS scores (P < 0.05). Group A achieved the highest 90-day favorable functional rate (69.0%), alongside minimal infarct progression and superior reperfusion (88.1%) (P < 0.001). Favorable HIR (OR = 3.274, P = 0.002) and collateral status (OR = 3.516, P = 0.001) were independent protective factors. The combined model (AUC = 0.84) exhibited better predictive performance than single-index evaluation. Group A also had lower sICH and 90-day mortality than Group D (P < 0.05). Combined HIR and collateral assessment offers a feasible imaging stratification approach for ultra-long-window LVO patients. Dual favorable imaging features predict favorable post-EVT efficacy and safety, assisting individualized clinical decision-making for delayed EVT candidates.

title: Transarterial endovascular treatment of tentorial dural arteriovenous fistulas: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: PURPOSE: To quantitatively evaluate the efficacy and safety of transarterial endovascular treatment for tentorial dural arteriovenous fistulas through a systematic review and meta-analysis. METHODS: A systematic review and single-arm meta-analysis were conducted according to PRISMA guidelines and Cochrane recommendations. PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were searched up to 10 December 2025, for studies reporting angiographic, clinical, and safety outcomes of transarterial endovascular treatment for tentorial dural arteriovenous fistulas. Pooled proportions with 95% confidence intervals (CI) were calculated using random-effects models, and heterogeneity was assessed using the I2 statistic, τ2, and Cochran's Q test. RESULTS: Ten independent observational cohorts comprised 450 patients, with extractable transarterial data for 371 and outcome-specific denominators. Pooled proportions were 81.2% (95% CI, 67.2-90.1%) for complete angiographic occlusion, 89.6% (82.1-94.1%) for favorable functional outcome, and 14.5% (9.7-21.0%) for overall complications. Among 161 patients, one procedure-related death and five all-cause deaths were reported; corresponding pooled proportions were 4.7% (2.0-11.0%) and 8.8% (4.1-17.9%). Mortality estimates were influenced by continuity corrections for zero-event studies. Disease-related mortality could not be separately quantified. CONCLUSION: TAE was associated with high pooled occlusion and favorable functional outcome proportions, alongside clinically relevant complications. Overall confidence in the evidence is low because of observational designs and methodological limitations; no randomized trials were included. Comparative efficacy and safety remain uncertain.

METHODS: A systematic review and single-arm meta-analysis were conducted according to PRISMA guidelines and Cochrane recommendations. PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were searched up to 10 December 2025, for studies reporting angiographic, clinical, and safety outcomes of transarterial endovascular treatment for tentorial dural arteriovenous fistulas.

title: Impact of chronic antiplatelet therapy on clinical outcomes of posterior circulation acute ischemic stroke.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Posterior circulation acute ischemic stroke (PCS) is a leading cause of neurologic disability, yet the hospital course of patients receiving chronic antiplatelet therapy (cAPT) remains unclear. This study evaluates the effect of cAPT on PCS outcomes, including patients undergoing endovascular thrombectomy (EVT). METHODS: This retrospective cross-sectional study used the National Inpatient Sample (2015-2022), including adult (≥18 years) hospitalizations in the United States for PCS with reported NIH Stroke Scale. Outcomes included inpatient mortality, routine discharge, complications, and receipt of reperfusion therapy. Propensity score-based inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) adjusted for confounding factors, including stroke severity. Multivariable logistic regression was used to estimate adjusted odds ratios (aORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs). RESULTS: p p p p p p p p p Among 148,740 PCS hospitalizations, 46,125 (31.0%) were receiving cAPT. These patients demonstrated reduced likelihood of undergoing intravascular thrombolysis (aOR: 0.902, 95% CI [0.835-0.975], = 0.009) and EVT (0.868 [0.764-0.987], = 0.031) compared to patients not on cAPT. Following IPTW, cAPT was associated with reduced inpatient mortality (0.581 [0.496-0.680], < 0.001) and increased routine discharge (1.14 [1.08-1.21], < 0.001). These patients also demonstrated reduced hemorrhagic transformation (0.767 [0.695-0.846], < 0.001) and cerebral edema/herniation (0.761 [0.698-0.831], < 0.001). Among hospitalizations undergoing EVT, cAPT was associated with reduced inpatient mortality (0.556 [0.408-0.757], < 0.001), increased routine discharge (1.60 [1.18-2.16], = 0.003), and reduced hemorrhagic transformation (0.778 [0.705-0.858], < 0.001). DISCUSSION: cAPT was associated with favorable inpatient outcomes in PCS, including lower mortality without an increased risk of serious neurological complications. Positive associations persisted among patients undergoing EVT. Prospective research is needed to confirm these results and guide therapeutic strategies.

METHODS: This retrospective cross-sectional study used the National Inpatient Sample (2015-2022), including adult (≥18 years) hospitalizations in the United States for PCS with reported NIH Stroke Scale.

title: Lunar phases, meteorological conditions, astrological signs, and postoperative outcomes of acute type A aortic dissection: Results of a retrospective cohort study.
abstract: p p p BackgroundAcute type A aortic dissection (ATAAD) is a surgical emergency associated with high mortality. While patient-related risk factors are well-established, beliefs persist regarding the influence of lunar phases, meteorological conditions, and astrological signs on disease occurrence and outcomes.MethodsWe retrospectively analysed all patients who underwent emergency surgery for ATAAD at Bordeaux University Hospital between 1996 and 2020. The primary objective was to assess the association between environmental factors (lunar phases, atmospheric pressure, temperature, and astrological signs) and ATAAD incidence. Secondary objectives included assessing their association with 30-day mortality and postoperative morbidity (intensive care unit length of stay, extracorporeal membrane oxygenation use, and mesenteric infarction). Meteorological data were available for 603 patients from 2010 onward.ResultsAmong 920 patients (70% male; mean age 63 ± 13 years), the 30-day mortality rate was 9.7%. Lunar phases were not associated with ATAAD incidence (first quarter 26%, last quarter 25%, new moon 25%, full moon 24%;= 0.91), mortality, or complications. Atmospheric pressure showed no association with ATAAD occurrence or outcomes. Temperature showed a weak correlation with ATAAD incidence (r = 0.11,= 0.01), but not with mortality. Astrological signs were not associated with ATAAD incidence, mortality, or morbidity. Longer cardiopulmonary bypass duration (odds ratio [OR] = 0.994 per minute; p = 0.01) and diabetes (OR = 4.63;= 0.01) were associated with 30-day mortality.ConclusionsEnvironmental factors were not associated with ATAAD incidence or outcomes. Established clinical factors remain the primary determinants of mortality.

title: An updated analysis of discharge opioid-prescribing patterns across surgical specialties in the USA.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Opioid overdose still accounts for substantial deaths and hospitalizations in the United States. Opioids continue to be commonly prescribed for postoperative pain. Although variation in postoperative opioid prescribing has been previously described, contemporary national data using newly available discharge-prescribing variables may provide useful benchmarks across surgical specialties and procedures. We sought to describe current patterns of opioid prescribing at discharge across surgical specialties and high-volume procedures in the United States. METHODS: This cross-sectional analysis used the 2024 American College of Surgeons National Surgical Quality Improvement Program (ACS-NSQIP) database and included adults undergoing selected procedures in the United States. The primary outcomes were the receipt of an opioid prescription at discharge and quantify the daily discharge opioid dose, expressed as morphine milligram equivalents per day (MME/day). RESULTS: Among 757,548 selected surgical procedures (mean [SD] age of patients, 56.35 [16.97] years; 441,799 [58.32%] female patients), 565,959 patients (74.71%) received an opioid prescription at discharge. Median daily opioid doses ranged from 30 to 45 MME/day across surgical specialties, and 4.1% of patients received a refill. Adjusted probabilities of receiving an opioid prescription at discharge varied by specialty: from 54.1% (95% CI 52.0%-55.9%) in cardiac surgery and 60.0% (95% CI 59.2%-60.7%) in vascular surgery to 84.3% (95% CI 84.1-84.5%) in orthopedics and 85.3% (95% CI, 84.7-85.9%) in thoracic surgery. Laparoscopic hernia repair, knee arthroplasty, hip arthroplasty, spine fusion, and laminectomy/corpectomy each had an adjusted probability of opioid prescription at discharge that exceeded 83%. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: This study provides an updated descriptive benchmark of postoperative opioid-prescribing patterns across surgical specialties and selected high-volume procedures. This evidence offers a foundation for strategic actions to reduce variation and improve patient care.

title: Prescribing Patterns of Extended Venous Thromboembolism Prophylaxis and VTE Incidence After Colorectal Cancer Resection: Insights From a Single Institution.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Patients undergoing colorectal cancer surgery are at increased risk for postoperative venous thromboembolism (VTE). Several societies recommend extended duration pharmacologic prophylaxis after discharge for selected high-risk patients, but real-world use is inconsistent, and the absolute benefit in the era of minimally invasive surgery and enhanced recovery remains uncertain. METHODS: We performed a retrospective cohort study of adults undergoing colon or rectal resection for cancer at a single academic center between 2020 and 2023. Patients receiving therapeutic anticoagulation, those with recent VTE or nonmalignant indications for surgery were excluded. Demographic, operative, and oncologic variables were collected along with inpatient and postdischarge VTE prophylaxis practices. Primary outcomes were (1) prescription of extended pharmacologic prophylaxis at discharge and (2) 90-d symptomatic VTE incidence. RESULTS: A total of 177 patients met the inclusion criteria. Most operations were minimally invasive and performed within an Enhanced Recovery After Surgery pathway. Despite the presence of traditional VTE risk factors, only a minority of patients were discharged on extended pharmacologic prophylaxis. Within 90 d, two patients developed symptomatic lower extremity deep vein thrombosis (1.1%); no pulmonary emboli or VTE events were identified. Both patients had high-risk features, including advanced age and emergent surgery. Routine screening imaging was not performed, and all events were clinically detected. CONCLUSIONS: In this enhanced recovery after surgery-based colorectal cancer cohort, extended postdischarge VTE prophylaxis was rarely prescribed; yet, the symptomatic VTE rate was low and limited to two high-risk individuals. These findings support a risk-stratified rather than universal approach to extended prophylaxis after colorectal surgery.

Several societies recommend extended duration pharmacologic prophylaxis after discharge for selected high-risk patients, but real-world use is inconsistent, and the absolute benefit in the era of minimally invasive surgery and enhanced recovery remains uncertain. METHODS: We performed a retrospective cohort study of adults undergoing colon or rectal resection for cancer at a single academic center between 2020 and 2023.

title: Association of admission aggregate index of systemic inflammation with lower-extremity deep vein thrombosis after severe trauma.
abstract: Early identification of patients at risk for lower-extremity deep vein thrombosis (LEDVT) after severe trauma remains difficult. This retrospective cohort study evaluated whether admission aggregate index of systemic inflammation (AISI), derived from platelet, neutrophil, monocyte, and lymphocyte counts, was associated with ultrasound-confirmed in-hospital LEDVT detected before the earlier of discharge or post-injury day 30 and whether it improved risk stratification. Among 223 adults with an Injury Severity Score of 16 or higher and evaluable bilateral lower-extremity ultrasonography, 93 (41.7%) had LEDVT. Each 1-SD increase in log-transformed AISI was associated with LEDVT after adjustment for age, sex, Injury Severity Score, Glasgow Coma Scale score, and shock index (odds ratio [OR], 2.07; 95% CI, 1.47-2.91; P < 0.001) and after additional adjustment for D-dimer, fibrin/fibrinogen degradation products, prothrombin time, activated partial thromboplastin time, and fibrinogen (OR, 1.86; 95% CI, 1.26-2.73; P = 0.002). Adding AISI to clinical variables increased the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) from 0.619 to 0.714 (AUC difference, 0.095; bootstrap 95% CI, 0.023 to 0.168; P = 0.009). After coagulation markers were included, the AUC difference was smaller and uncertain (0.018; 95% CI, -0.010 to 0.046; P = 0.166), although the Brier score improved by 0.014 (P = 0.020). For Model 4, bootstrap-corrected and repeated-cross-validation AUCs were 0.797 and 0.790, and calibration slopes were 0.831 and 0.773, respectively. With 93 events and 11 candidate parameters, these internally validated results indicate shrinkage and require prospective external validation; AISI should be interpreted as a complementary admission marker.

title: Anesthetic technique is associated with complication risk and healthcare utilization following total shoulder arthroplasty.
abstract: PURPOSE: Compare perioperative complications and healthcare utilization among total shoulder arthroplasty (TSA) patients receiving general (GA), regional (RA), or combined anesthesia (RA + GA). METHODS: Using the TriNetX database, patients undergoing primary TSA were identified and stratified into three groups based on anesthetic technique: GA, RA, and combined RA + GA. 1:1 Propensity score matching was performed to using the GA cohort as reference to control for baseline demographic and clinical covariates. Outcomes of interest included 90-day complication rates including UTI, venous thromboembolism (VTE), acute kidney injury (AKI), prosthetic joint infection (PJI), pneumonia, constipation, and revision TSA, emergency department (ED) visits and hospital readmission, Foley catheter insertion, postoperative opioid prescriptions and mean opioid number of prescriptions. Statistical significance was set at p < 0.05. RESULTS: Comparing GA with RA, each cohort consisted of 28,564 patients. RA was associated with lower rates of UTI, AKI, constipation, pneumonia, fewer patients prescribed opioids and fewer opioid prescriptions per patient while being associated with increased healthcare utilization compared to GA alone. Comparing RA + GA with GA alone, 17,926 matched patients were included in each cohort. RA + GA was associated with lower rates of UTI and opioid prescriptions, and higher rates of healthcare utilization compared to GA alone. CONCLUSION: These findings suggest that while RA provides early analgesic and opioid-sparing benefits after TSA, it is associated with increased post-operative healthcare utilization. These findings help guide surgical decision making and highlight the need for standardized perioperative protocols to optimize postoperative pain control and manage rebound pain-related care utilization with RA techniques. LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: III.

title: Exploratory topological modeling of reported frequencies of aortic arch branching variations.
abstract: Anatomical variations in the branching patterns of the aortic arch affect endovascular access, surgical planning, and cerebral perfusion strategies. However, the quantitative relationship between branching topology and the frequency distribution of these variations remains unclear. The study aimed to explore whether topological differences among final aortic arch branching configurations are associated with their reported frequencies. Seven pooled type-level frequency estimates from a published meta-analysis were analyzed. Node-Shift and Edge-Loss-Change Scores were defined from the final branching topology relative to Type 1 (separate brachiocephalic, left common carotid, and left subclavian origins from a left-sided arch). A three-parameter log-linear model was fitted by ordinary least squares to natural-log-transformed frequencies. Leave-one-out cross-validation and sensitivity analyses by study modality, study size, and exclusion of Type 1 or Type 4 (common brachiocephalic-left common carotid origin with a left vertebral artery arising directly from the arch) were performed. The fitted log-linear model had an intercept of 4.491 and coefficients of -2.751 for the Node-Shift Score and - 5.474 for the Edge-Loss-Change Score. The coefficient of determination was 0.932 on the log-frequency scale and 0.974 after back-transformation to the original frequency scale. Leave-one-out Q² values were 0.821 and 0.778 on the log and original scales, respectively. Coefficients remained negative in imaging-only, cadaveric-only, studies with at least 100 specimens, Type 1-excluded, and Type 4-excluded analyses. Within this seven-type aggregated dataset, configurations with larger topological scores had lower reported frequencies. The proposed scores provide a compact exploratory description of branching variation, but the model does not establish a developmental mechanism, predict individual anatomy, or support direct clinical decision-making without external validation.

However, the quantitative relationship between branching topology and the frequency distribution of these variations remains unclear. The study aimed to explore whether topological differences among final aortic arch branching configurations are associated with their reported frequencies.

title: Preoperative prevalence and risk factors for thromboembolic events following tibial plateau fractures: a retrospective analysis of an underestimated risk.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Tibial plateau fractures (TPF) are complex intra-articular injuries carrying a high risk of deep vein thrombosis (DVT), muscular vein thrombosis (MVT) and pulmonary embolism (PE). Preoperative thrombosis is frequently clinically silent yet may cause serious complications, whereas its detection delays definitive surgery. This study assessed the prevalence and risk factors of preoperative venous thromboembolic events (VTE) in surgically treated TPF before and after implementation of routine duplex ultrasound screening. METHODS: In this retrospective single-centre study at a level 1 trauma centre, all adult patients surgically treated for traumatic TPF (AO 41B/C) between January 2015 and August 2025 were reviewed (547 patients, 554 fractures). Until August 2020 duplex ultrasound (DUS) was performed only on clinical suspicion; from August 2020 onward routine preoperative DUS was progressively implemented. VTE were confirmed by DUS or CT angiography. Prevalences are reported per fracture and patient characteristics per patient; regression analyses were performed at fracture level, except for the patient-related model. RESULTS: With DUS restricted to clinical suspicion (cohort A; 246 fractures), the detected prevalence of preoperative VTE was 3.7% (95% CI 1.9-6.8) and that of DVT 2.4% (1.1-5.2). Under routine screening (cohort B; 205 screened fractures) it was 20.0% (15.1-26.0) and 17.1% (12.5-22.8), respectively, 82.9% of DVT being distal. Given the different diagnostic strategies, this reflects the higher diagnostic yield of screening rather than a true increase in VTE. In cohort B, 28 of 41 VTE (68.3%) and 24 of 35 DVT (68.6%) were clinically silent. Two patients had in-hospital cardiac arrest from PE: one died from a DVT undetected before screening was introduced, the other had an asymptomatic DVT identified by screening. VTE was independently associated with pre-existing therapeutic anticoagulation (adjusted OR 2.96, 95% CI 1.10-7.98) and with the duration of external fixation (adjusted OR 1.11 per day, 1.02-1.20). High-grade closed soft-tissue injury (adjusted OR 2.41, 1.07-5.45), polytrauma (adjusted OR 2.24, 1.07-4.68) and initial external fixation (univariable OR 3.60, 1.76-7.35) were also associated with VTE, but none remained significant after accounting for fixation duration (adjusted OR 1.42, 0.52-3.89; 1.96, 0.76-5.05; 0.62, 0.12-3.27), i.e. risk was driven by time in the fixator rather than by external fixation as such. CONCLUSIONS: Surgically treated TPF carry a substantial burden of preoperative VTE, and routine DUS reveals a high proportion of clinically silent thrombosis that would otherwise remain undetected. Severe closed soft-tissue injury, pre-existing therapeutic anticoagulation and, above all, the duration of external fixation may help to identify patients at increased risk. As two diagnostic rather than two treatment strategies were compared, the study cannot determine whether screening improves outcomes or reduces PE; prospective evaluation of structured screening and risk-adapted thromboprophylaxis is warranted.

Preoperative thrombosis is frequently clinically silent yet may cause serious complications, whereas its detection delays definitive surgery. This study assessed the prevalence and risk factors of preoperative venous thromboembolic events (VTE) in surgically treated TPF before and after implementation of routine duplex ultrasound screening.

title: Artificial intelligence in varicose veins: Comparative insights from other vascular diseases, evidence gaps, and future prospects.
abstract: This review provides a comprehensive overview of the performance of artificial intelligence (AI) in varicose veins (VV), covering applications in image recognition, postoperative management, risk factor and biomarker analysis, and the use of large language models (LLMs) to aid clinical decision-making. While significant advancements have been made, valuable lessons can be drawn from AI applications in other vascular diseases. Key considerations for advancing AI in VV include ensuring methodological rigor, high quality data, external validation, strict attention to data security and legal standards, and linking AI tools to clinically important outcomes. It is recommended that machine learning models be developed and validated within standardized frameworks that future VV research can adopt. Accordingly, the development of clear guidelines and benchmarks is imperative. LLMs hold promise in relieving clinicians of repetitive routine tasks, thereby enhancing diagnostic accuracy and assisting in treatment planning. Additionally, LLM-based tools could support the curation of medical content on short video platforms and assist clinicians in creating educational materials, ultimately improving patient engagement and understanding.

title: ® ® Comparative cost analysis of Eluvia™ versus ZilverPTXin treating femoropopliteal peripheral artery disease utilizing real-world data.
abstract: Aim: Materials & methods: Results: Conclusion: ® ® To compare the hospital-based costs among patients with femoropopliteal artery (FPA) disease treated with Eluvia™ versus ZilverPTXdrug-eluting stents using a large real-world USA hospital database.This retrospective study included adults in the Premier Healthcare Database who underwent lower extremity FPA endovascular revascularization with Eluvia or Zilver PTX between 1 April 2019 and 31 March 2022. Total hospital-based costs during the index procedure and cumulative 1- and 2-year post-discharge follow-up were compared using multivariable generalized linear models adjusted for age, sex, race and baseline chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) status. Prespecified subgroup analyses were conducted by care setting (hospital inpatient and hospital outpatient) and among patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) and CLTI.A total of 7208 patients were included, comprising 4218 treated with Eluvia and 2990 treated with Zilver PTX. Patients treated with Eluvia had a higher prevalence of several comorbidities, including congestive heart failure and CKD. Unadjusted mean hospital-based index procedure costs were similar between groups (Eluvia, $28,631 vs Zilver PTX, $28,359; difference, -$272; p = 0.7233). After adjustment, mean index procedure hospital-based costs did not differ significantly between treatment groups ($30,031, p = 0.8491). However, Eluvia was associated with lower adjusted cumulative hospital-based costs at the 1-year (difference, $4,017; p = 0.0066) and 2-year (difference, $6250; p = 0.0021) follow-up. Similar associations were observed in the hospital inpatient and CKD subgroups, whereas no statistically significant differences were observed in the CLTI subgroup.Across patients undergoing femoropopliteal endovascular revascularization, Eluvia was associated with significantly lower post-discharge cumulative hospital-based follow-up costs than Zilver PTX while index procedure costs were comparable. These findings reflect hospital-based costs captured within participating hospitals and do not include medication costs or costs of care received outside the Premier Healthcare Database; therefore, they should not be interpreted as total healthcare costs.

title: Continuity of Chronic Wound Care Across Hospital-to-Home Transitions: A Qualitative Study of Hospital and Community Nurses' Experiences.
abstract: AimTo explore how hospital nurses (HNs) and community nurses (CNs) in France manage chronic wound care for older adults across settings, and how their practices shape continuity of care during hospital-to-home transitions.DesignQualitative descriptive study combining ethnographic shadowing and a focus group.MethodsFieldwork took place in a French university hospital, across four units: acute geriatrics, rehabilitation, vascular surgery, dermatology. The focus group involved CNs from seven different self-employed nursing practices. We shadowed 15 HNs for approximately 92 h and conducted one focus group with 7 CNs. Data were analyzed inductively using constant comparison, with a second-stage interpretive analysis informed by Meleis' transitions theory.ResultsFour interconnected processes shaped continuity of chronic wound care across the transition: (1) nursing expertise in wound management was expressed differently across hospital and community settings; (2) discharge coordination was fragmented, with rare nurse-to-nurse communication and insufficient transfer of wound-specific information; (3) organizational logics diverged, with discontinuous hospital workflows and time-pressured, fee-for-service-constrained community visits; and (4) patient involvement during hospitalization was limited, constraining engagement and preparedness post-discharge. Continuity was frequently maintained through compensatory work from nurses.ConclusionContinuity of chronic wound care depends less on nursing expertise than on the organizational conditions enabling that expertise to be mobilized across settings.ImpactThis study highlights the need for more integrated transitional care, including clearer and more consistent responsibilities at discharge, structured nurse-to-nurse discharge communication, and earlier patient involvement in wound care management.

title: Prostatic Artery Embolization in a Patient With Bilateral Internal Iliac Artery Occlusions.
abstract: Background: Study Sample: Results: Conclusions: Prostatic artery embolization (PAE) is an established treatment for lower urinary tract symptoms due to benign prostatic hyperplasia but can be challenging in complex anatomy.An 86-year-old male with history of abdominal aortic aneurysm repair and aortobifemoral bypass presented with gross hematuria and urinary retention. Imaging and clinical evaluation confirmed BPH-related clot retention as the etiology. Careful review of preprocedural CT angiography revealed occluded bilateral internal iliac arteries, a right aberrant obturator artery (AOA) (corona mortis variant), arising from the inferior epigastric artery, which itself originated from the native right external iliac artery. The AOA supplied the entire prostate, perfusing both lobes and contributing to the contralateral pelvic circulation as well. Cone-beam CT and angiography confirmed the perfusion to both prostatic lobes. PAE was performed by accessing the native common femoral artery and selectively catheterizing the AOA. Embolization of the prostatic parenchyma was completed successfully while preserving flow to adjacent pelvic structures, avoiding non-target embolization.The patient had complete resolution of hematuria and urinary retention and remained catheter-free at 1-year follow-up.This case highlights the importance of pre-procedural evaluation and planning, demonstrating that PAE can be safely and effectively performed even in variant vascular anatomy.

title: Use of a central venous catheter as vascular access at the start of a regular hemodialysis program: impact on mortality over 2 years.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The recommended access for starting chronic hemodialysis (HD) is an arteriovenous fistula (AVF), but a (CVC) continues to be frequently used. Worldwide, its use has been associated with higher mortality, but data from Brazil are lacking. METHODS: Analytical, observational, and retrospective cohort study that aimed at analyzing the data available in the Brazilian Monthly Dialysis Registry database from Jan/2011 to Dec/2023. Using data from this registry, we evaluated the frequency of CVC use (regardless of whether tunneled or non-tunneled) at the start of HD across 13 years and assessed its impact on all-cause mortality over 2 years. RESULTS: We studied 10,182 patients. The mean age was 59 (47-69) years; 59% were male, and 33% had diabetes. CVC use at HD entry increased substantially in the last 10 years. The 2-year mortality rates for CVC and primary AVF/graft users were 20% and 9%, respectively, P < 0.001. In the fully adjusted multivariate model, the use of CVC persisted significantly associated with mortality (HR 1.69, 95%CI 1.23-2.25, P=0.001). Other variables directly associated with mortality were age (HR 1.04, 95%CI 1.03-1.05, P=0.001), and serum ferritin (HR 1.18, 95%CI 1.06-1.30, P=0.002). Serum albumin (HR 0.86, 95%CI 0.84-0.88, P<0.001) and URR (HR 0.97, 95%CI 0.96-0.97, P<0.001) emerged as protective factors. CONCLUSIONS: CVC use was associated with a 1.69-fold increased risk of 2-year mortality. The increasing use of CVCs in Brazil is concerning and highlights the need for public health strategies promoting timely permanent vascular access before HD initiation.

title: Ultrasound-guided cyanoacrylate embolization of refluxing tributaries during truncal cyanoacrylate closure (SLICE): Technique description and a proof-of-concept feasibility study.
abstract: p ObjectivesTruncal cyanoacrylate closure (CAC) does not treat refluxing tributary varicosities. We describe Side-branch Local Injection of Cyanoacrylate Embolization (SLICE) - ultrasound-guided injection of the VenaSeal adhesive into refluxing tributaries during truncal CAC - and assess its technical feasibility and periprocedural safety.MethodsSingle-center retrospective review of 32 consecutive patients (49 limbs, 58 truncal veins) treated by truncal CAC between September 2024 and December 2025; SLICE was performed in 14. The primary endpoint was technical success, defined as the absence of reflux within an injected tributary on the first postoperative duplex study. Secondary endpoints included 3-month durability, truncal occlusion, and adverse events.Results22 refluxing tributaries were injected; all were epifascial, at a median depth of 4.0 mm (range 1.2-9.6). A median of four dispenser trigger pulls was used per site (range 3-8); the series was underpowered to relate pull count to diameter (Spearman rho -0.16,= 0.50). Technical success was 21/22 (95%; 95% confidence interval 77.2-99.9) initially and 19/20 (95%; 75.1-99.9) at 3 months. On 3-month computed tomography (CT), 14 of 17 evaluable injected tributaries were occluded whereas 16 of 17 were free of reflux: anatomical occlusion lagged behind hemodynamic success. Truncal occlusion was preserved (30/30 at 1 week; 26/27 at 3 months). There was no phlebitis, deep vein thrombosis, pulmonary embolism, or adhesive removal. Hyperpigmentation occurred in 3/14 patients, all with an injection <2 mm below the skin; two mild delayed hypersensitivity reactions occurred, both over the truncal rather than an injected site. One patient (7%) required re-intervention.ConclusionsSLICE is technically feasible and reproducible within a narrow range of adhesive delivery, with no adhesive-related complication at an injected site in this small series with short follow-up. Prospective comparative evaluation with patient-centered endpoints is required before efficacy can be claimed.

title: Electrosurgical septotomy across the full spectrum of aortic dissection.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: Transcatheter electrosurgical septotomy divides the dissection membrane to reconstitute a single aortic lumen. Reported experience is largely confined to chronic post-dissection aneurysms. We assessed the technique across the full spectrum of descending aortic dissection, including stand-alone treatment of malperfusion. METHODS: Retrospective intention-to-treat analysis of 21 consecutive patients scheduled for septotomy between June 2022 and May 2026. The membrane was crossed by needle re-entry and divided with an electrified through-and-through guidewire at 40-60 W under fluoroscopy, without routine intravascular ultrasound or image fusion. A perfused-lumen index (perfused lumen divided by total aortic diameter) was measured before and after the procedure. RESULTS: Septotomy was performed in 20 of 21 patients (technical success 95% on an intention-to-treat basis). Indications were landing-zone preparation (57%), malperfusion (33%), preparation for open repair and true-lumen collapse. Malperfusion resolved in all 7 patients treated for that indication, and the perfused-lumen index rose from a median of 0.16 to 0.98 (18 patients, P < 0.001). There was no stroke, spinal cord ischaemia or retrograde type A dissection. Thirty-day, in-hospital and overall mortality were 10%, 14% and 19%, with one fatal delayed aortic rupture and no intraprocedural death. Three unplanned reinterventions occurred; median follow-up was 5.1 months. CONCLUSIONS: Electrosurgical septotomy was feasible across the full spectrum of aortic dissection and, in selected patients, as stand-alone treatment for malperfusion, using standard electrosurgical equipment. Given the small heterogeneous cohort and short follow-up, these findings demonstrate feasibility rather than durability.

Reported experience is largely confined to chronic post-dissection aneurysms. We assessed the technique across the full spectrum of descending aortic dissection, including stand-alone treatment of malperfusion.

title: Aspiration Thrombectomy for High-Risk Pulmonary Embolism With Life-Threatening Anemia and Active Uterine Bleeding: A Case Report.
abstract: BACKGROUND High-risk pulmonary embolism (PE) carries significant mortality, and management becomes complex when it coexists with severe anemia and active bleeding, as thrombolysis is then contraindicated. We report the case of a patient with high-risk PE complicated by severe anemia (hemoglobin 41 g/L) and active uterine bleeding from adenomyosis. CASE REPORT A 48-year-old woman presented with haemodynamic instability (blood pressure 74/47 mm Hg), critical anemia (hemoglobin 41 g/L), and a 3-year history of irregular vaginal bleeding from adenomyosis. Computed tomography (CT) pulmonary angiography confirmed bilateral PE with right pulmonary artery main-trunk occlusion; echocardiography showed severe pulmonary hypertension, and duplex ultrasound showed extensive left lower-limb deep vein thrombosis. Thrombolysis was contraindicated. Emergency percutaneous aspiration thrombectomy was performed using large-bore catheters (22F, 20F, 16F) with concurrent inferior vena cava filter placement, reducing pulmonary artery pressure from 51/23 to 34/12 mm Hg; the estimated blood loss, quantified from filtered aspirate, was approximately 100 mL. Adjuncts included transfusion of 13 units of packed red cells, dilatation and curettage, gonadotropin-releasing hormone agonist therapy, and titrated anticoagulation. At discharge after a 24-day hospitalization she was hemodynamically stable, and free of dyspnea, with resolved edema and hemoglobin 72 g/L, on oral rivaroxaban. CONCLUSIONS In this thrombolysis-contraindicated patient, aspiration thrombectomy with inferior vena cava filter placement was a feasible rescue strategy that achieved rapid hemodynamic and angiographic improvement without thrombolysis, with palliative rather than curative intent. As a single case, it cannot establish comparative safety or efficacy, and broader conclusions regarding efficacy cannot be drawn. It illustrates a potentially useful approach in similarly complex scenarios where coordinated multidisciplinary care is essential.

title: Adiposity and the risk of aortic dissection incidence and mortality: results from the UK Biobank, the J-SHC study and a meta-analysis of cohort studies.
abstract: trend trend trend trend trend trend trend trend trend trend 2 2 2 2 Few studies have investigated the association between adiposity and risk of aortic dissection and data is lacking on adiposity measures other than body mass index (BMI). We analyzed the association between adiposity and risk of aortic dissection in the UK Biobank, and the Japan Specific Health Checkups (J-SHC) Study, and conducted a meta-analysis of cohort studies to clarify the associations between adiposity and risk of aortic dissection. The analytical cohorts included 496,255 participants in the UK Biobank and 630,841 participants in the J-SHC Study. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression models were used to analyze associations between adiposity and risk of aortic dissection. PubMed and Embase were searched for relevant studies up to February 27, 2026. Random effects models were used to calculate summary relative risks (RRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for the association between adiposity and risk of aortic dissection. In the UK Biobank and J-SHC, there were 371 and 105 aortic dissections during 12.3 and 4 years follow-up, respectively. In the UK Biobank, positive associations (HRs, 95% CIs) were observed between high BMI (1.54, 1.01-2.37, p=0.01), waist circumference (1.82, 1.27-2.60, p=0.001), hip circumference (1.77, 1.25-2.50, p<0.001), waist-to-height ratio (1.88, 1.30-2.70, p=0.10), and fat mass (1.36, 0.97-1.91, p=0.02) and aortic dissection risk, but no clear association was observed for waist-to-hip ratio (1.28, 0.90-1.81, p=0.08) and body fat percentage (1.09, 0.77-1.54, p=0.53). In the J-SHC Study, higher BMI (2.36, 0.98-4.84, p=0.018), waist circumference (2.26, 1.18-4.60, p=0.003), and waist-to-height ratio (2.61, 1.27-5.92, p=0.009) were positively associated with aortic dissection mortality. Five cohort studies were included in the meta-analysis on BMI and aortic dissection (2007 cases and 4,962,288 participants). The summary RR per 5 kg/mincrement in BMI was 1.09 (1.00-1.20, I = 43%), per 10 cm increment in waist circumference was 1.21 (1.05-1.40, I = 50%, n = 2), and per 0.1 unit increment in waist-to-height ratio was 1.32 (1.08-1.61, I = 39%, n = 2). These findings provide evidence for a positive association between both general and abdominal adiposity and the risk of aortic dissection, with the strongest associations observed for high waist-to-height ratio. Although further large-scale studies are warranted for confirmation, these findings suggest avoiding excess weight may be an important strategy for the prevention of aortic dissection.

title: Beyond stroke: atrial fibrillation and the broader burden of thromboembolic events in the population-based EpiHealth study.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: To investigate the distribution and risk of thromboembolic events (TEs) among adults with and without atrial fibrillation (AF), and to assess oral anticoagulant (OAC) use over time. DESIGN: This population-based longitudinal cohort study included EpiHealth participants recruited between April 2011 and December 2016 and followed through linkage to Swedish health data registers from baseline until the first TE, death, or December 31, 2016. RESULTS: p At baseline, 873 of 22,616 participants (3.9%) had AF and 297 developed incident AF during follow-up. 484 participants experienced at least one TE during 70,587 person-years. Participants with AF had higher TE incidence (68 events, 5.9%; < 0.001), predominantly arterial (73.5%), with 94% of arterial events involving the cerebral circulation. Approximately one quarter of TEs among participants with AF occurred outside the cerebral circulation and comprised both venous and non-cerebral arterial events. Although participants with incident AF represented less than one quarter of participants with AF, they accounted for 40% of TEs in the AF group. OAC use increased from 39.0% to 50.4%, with a shift from predominantly warfarin to direct oral anticoagulants. In time-dependent Cox regression adjusted for age, sex, and prior arterial thromboembolism, untreated AF was associated with increased thromboembolic risk compared with no AF (HR 2.53), whereas OAC use was associated with lower risk. CONCLUSIONS: AF was associated with substantially increased thromboembolic risk, predominantly arterial in nature. One in five TEs among participants with AF coincided with newly diagnosed AF, suggesting potential opportunities for earlier AF detection and timely initiation of anticoagulant treatment.

title: Long-term outcome of stenting for the iliac vein stenosis with ipsilateral arterio-venous graft; a case series.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To analyze the possible etiology and evaluate the technical and clinical outcomes of using bare metal stents for the treatment of central venous stenosis (CVS) in the lower extremity with ipsilateral hemodialysis access. METHODS: A single-center retrospective analysis of a small case series was conducted in hemodialysis patients with lower extremity arteriovenous grafts (AVG) who were treated with bare metal stents (BMS) for symptomatic iliac vein stenosis between April 2016 and June 2021. Patients' demographic data, technical details, adverse events, clinical outcomes, and imaging data were recorded. RESULTS: The study cohort comprised seven females and four males, with a mean age of 58.8 ± 13.4 years. Preoperative lower limb venography was performed in nine patients scheduled for AVG creation. With the exception of one case demonstrating left iliac vein compression, the iliac veins were patent in all other patients. Symptoms of lower limb swelling developed at a mean interval of 9.40 ± 5.83 months (range: 3-20 months) following AVG placement. Eight cases had a concomitant history of temporary ipsilateral femoral vein catheterization. Lesion characteristics included nine stenotic lesions and two occlusive lesions. All patients were treated with SMART Control stents (Cordis Corp, USA). The technical success rate was 100%, and symptomatic relief was achieved in all cases. Over a mean follow-up period of 47.8 ± 31.7 months (range: 10-123 months), the target lesion primary patency was 100% (one-side confidence interval [CI] = 0.74,1). CONCLUSIONS: Using BMS is a safe and effective method to treat iliac vein stenosis with ipsilateral AVG.

METHODS: A single-center retrospective analysis of a small case series was conducted in hemodialysis patients with lower extremity arteriovenous grafts (AVG) who were treated with bare metal stents (BMS) for symptomatic iliac vein stenosis between April 2016 and June 2021. Patients' demographic data, technical details, adverse events, clinical outcomes, and imaging data were recorded.

title: Bilateral peripheral CT venography for evaluating central venous lesions in dysfunctional arteriovenous fistulas: feasibility, safety, and radiation dose in hemodialysis patients.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: Central venous stenosis and occlusion are major causes of arteriovenous fistula (AVF) dysfunction in hemodialysis patients. This study aimed to evaluate the feasibility, safety, radiation exposure, and anatomical findings of bilateral peripheral CT venography for central venous assessment in patients with dysfunctional AVFs. METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study included 46 consecutive hemodialysis patients with dysfunctional AVFs who underwent bilateral peripheral CT venography between August 2023 and June 2025. Technical success, procedure-related adverse events, radiation dose parameters, central venous lesion characteristics, and agreement with available comparative imaging modalities were analyzed. Comparative imaging findings from puncture-based angiography and/or duplex ultrasonography were assessed descriptively. RESULTS: All 46 examinations were technically successful (100%), with a mean procedure duration of 4 minutes (range, 3-5 minutes). Minor adverse events included one patient of contrast extravasation (2.2%) and 3 of mild allergic reactions (6.5%); no severe procedure-related complications were documented. The mean CTDIvol and DLP were 11.87 mGy and 784.15 mGy·cm, respectively. Central venous abnormalities were identified in 44 patients (95.7%), including stenosis in 31 (67.4%), occlusion in 11 (23.9%), and aneurysmal changes in 2 (4.3%). Comparative imaging was available in 38 patients, and CT venography showed agreement with available findings in 37 cases (97.4%). This agreement was interpreted as descriptive concordance rather than formal diagnostic accuracy. CONCLUSIONS: Bilateral peripheral CT venography demonstrated high technical feasibility, acceptable safety, and effective visualization of central venous abnormalities in hemodialysis patients with dysfunctional AVFs. Further prospective studies are needed to validate its diagnostic performance and clinical impact. ADVANCES IN KNOWLEDGE: This technique enables efficient, noninvasive assessment of central venous pathology with minimal risk, supporting its potential as a practical alternative to conventional imaging in hemodialysis patients.

title: Aortic Dissection Incidentally Detected on PET/CT During Evaluation for Suspected Multiple Myeloma.
abstract: The identification and diagnosis of aortic dissection on PET/CT remain challenging without the use of contrast agents. Such cases are prone to misdiagnosis or being overlooked, particularly when the examination is focused on an unrelated primary clinical objective. We present a case of thoracic aortic dissection that was incidentally detected on initial PET/CT during the further evaluation of suspected multiple myeloma. The FDG-avid lesion was initially mistaken for an esophageal mass, with differential diagnoses including extramedullary plasmacytoma associated with multiple myeloma and primary esophageal neoplasm.
