title: Anatomical Variations of Renal Arteries: Clinical, Radiological, and Surgical Considerations.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To synthesize the current knowledge regarding the embryological basis, anatomical classification, imaging characterization, and clinical implications of accessory renal arteries. BACKGROUND: Anatomical variations in the renal arteries are common, affecting approximately 20-35% of the population, and have significant implications for clinical outcomes and surgical planning. Accessory renal arteries are usually terminal vessels that serve discrete renal islands with minimal collateral circulation in the body; therefore, their preoperative identification is important. However, there has been no modern synthesis of embryology, imaging, and multidisciplinary clinical treatment for these variations. METHODS: A narrative review of the literature was conducted by searching PubMed and Google Scholar for publications from December 2015 to December 2025. MeSH terms and free-text keywords related to "accessory renal artery," "multiple renal arteries," "renal artery variations," "renal vascular anatomy," "kidney transplantation," "renovascular hypertension," "computed tomography angiography," "magnetic resonance angiography," and "endovascular aortic repair" were used in Boolean combinations. Peer-reviewed original studies, systematic reviews, meta-analyses, and case series were included. Conference abstracts, unpublished data, and non-English publications were excluded. DISCUSSION: This review addresses the embryological basis and anatomical classification of accessory renal arteries; the diagnostic roles of Doppler ultrasound, computed tomography angiography, and magnetic resonance angiography; and their clinical implications in kidney transplantation, partial nephrectomy, and endovascular aortic repair, including the contested association with renovascular hypertension. Available data suggest that most accessory vessels do not independently cause hypertension, whereas stenosis of larger vessels may be a correctable etiology in selected cases. CONCLUSION: Accessory renal arteries have a significant clinical impact, primarily determined by the size of the vessels and the area of the kidney they supply. Preoperative characterization based on modern imaging can be reliable and can help plan and manage surgery for each patient. More prospective research is required to establish evidence-based principles for vessel maintenance and evaluate new technologies in this context.

title: When not to explore: a combat-specific decision framework for selective neck exploration at Role 2.
abstract: Current civilian algorithms for penetrating neck trauma assume access to definitive vascular reconstruction, endovascular intervention, advanced imaging, and specialist multidisciplinary care. These assumptions may not apply to Role 2 military facilities, where neck exploration can commit the surgeon to procedures that cannot be completed under optimal conditions. This position paper was developed through a focused narrative review of contemporary recommendations and literature on penetrating neck trauma, vascular and aerodigestive injury, temporary hemorrhage control, and combat casualty care, supplemented by targeted PubMed searches addressing penetrating carotid injury, temporary vascular shunting, carotid collateral circulation, aerodigestive trauma, balloon tamponade, and Role 2-to-Role 3 evacuation. We propose a combat-specific framework distinguishing injuries requiring immediate surgery from those in which temporary hemorrhage control, airway protection, stabilization, and evacuation may better preserve definitive treatment options. The framework challenges automatic application of selected civilian indications for neck exploration in stable patients when hemorrhage is controlled and safe evacuation is feasible, extends this selective approach to aerodigestive injuries, and incorporates transport conditions and en-route rescue capability into the decision to operate. We also propose hypotheses regarding common carotid artery shunting, including the potential effects of collateral cerebral perfusion, shunt position, configuration, monitoring limitations, and thromboembolic complications on neurological outcomes. Role 2 decision-making should incorporate surgical capability, physiology, airway security, effectiveness of temporary hemorrhage control, and evacuation feasibility. Safe evacuation depends not only on transport time but also on the reliability of temporary control and the ability to manage deterioration en route. Rather than replacing civilian algorithms, this framework adapts them to combat casualty care while introducing hypotheses requiring prospective clinical and experimental validation.

title: Traditional Chinese medicine for diabetic lower extremity arterial disease: A review of recent advances.
abstract: Diabetic lower-extremity arterial disease (LEAD) is a prevalent macrovascular complication of diabetes and a critical pathological foundation for diabetic foot lesions. Its pathogenesis involves glycolipid metabolic disturbance, excessive oxidative stress, persistent vascular inflammation, and endothelial dysfunction, leading to limb ischemia, refractory foot ulcers, and increased amputation risk. Current standard treatments, including glycemic and lipid control, antiplatelet therapy, and endovascular revascularization, have improved clinical outcomes but still face challenges in fully ameliorating microcirculatory impairment and preventing long-term restenosis. Traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) exerts multi-component and multi-target protective effects against diabetic LEAD. This review summarizes pharmacological advances in representative TCM agents, including Salvia miltiorrhiza, Astragali Radix, and their bioactive constituents (e.g., tanshinone IIA sulfonate, salvianolic acid B, astragaloside IV, and Astragalus polysaccharide), as well as classical formulas and patent medicines such as Huangqi Guizhi Wuwu Decoction, Tongxinluo capsule, Tangbi capsule, and Danggui Sini Decoction. Their mechanisms involve protecting vascular endothelium, regulating glycolipid metabolism, suppressing vascular inflammation via NF-κB and NLRP3 pathways, and activating Nrf2-mediated antioxidant defense, HIF-1α/VEGF, PI3K-AKT, and Ang-1/Tie-2 signaling to restore microcirculation and promote angiogenesis. Clinically, TCM-assisted endovascular intervention reduces postoperative restenosis and improves lower-limb perfusion; external preparations promote diabetic foot ulcer healing; acupuncture, moxibustion, and mind-body exercises improve microcirculation and long-term management. TCM is a promising adjunctive strategy for diabetic LEAD, and further mechanistic and clinical studies are needed to advance its standardized application and improve patient prognosis.

title: Microsurgical Ligation of Spinal Dural Arteriovenous Fistula.
abstract: Spinal dural arteriovenous fistulas are a reversible cause of progressive thoracic myelopathy, for which definitive treatment requires complete disconnection of the pathological arteriovenous shunt. We demonstrate microsurgical clip occlusion and disconnection of a right T4 spinal dural arteriovenous fistula using indocyanine green (ICG) videoangiography and intraoperative neuromonitoring. Following T4-T5 laminectomy, the fistulous point was identified near the right T4 nerve root exit zone, with ICG confirming arterialized venous drainage. A clip was placed immediately adjacent to the dural fistulous point, and repeat ICG demonstrated obliteration of the shunt. The draining vein was subsequently coagulated and divided, with stable somatosensory and motor evoked potentials throughout the procedure. Precise angiographic localization and disconnection as close as possible to the dural fistulous point are critical to minimize residual shunting, vascular recruitment, and recurrence. ICG videoangiography and neuromonitoring provide valuable intraoperative confirmation for safe and definitive microsurgical treatment.

title: Microsurgical Clipping of a Posterior Communicating Artery-Incorporated Internal Carotid-Posterior Communicating Artery Aneurysm using Patient-Specific Three-Dimensional Aneurysm Models.
abstract: BACKGROUND AND INTRODUCTION: Posterior communicating artery (PCoA)-incorporated aneurysms, in which the PCoA originates from the dome, have a higher recurrence rate after endovascular treatment. Clipping is effective but technically demanding as the PCoA origin is frequently obscured by the internal carotid artery (ICA). OBJECTIVE: We present a video demonstrating microsurgical clipping of a posteriorly projecting PCoA-incorporated aneurysm using a patient-specific 3D-printed model. SURGICAL TECHNIQUE: Preoperative simulation predicted ICA obstruction of the PCoA origin. The aneurysm was dissected through the retrocarotid and opticocarotid spaces, and clips were sequentially applied, preserving the PCoA and its perforators. Indocyanine green videoangiography confirmed complete obliteration with PCoA patency. RESULT: The postoperative course was uneventful, and angiography confirmed successful clipping. CONCLUSION: Microsurgical clipping is a promising, safe, and effective alternative for PCoA-incorporated aneurysms. PEARLS AND PITFALLS: Preoperative simulation with a patient-specific 3D-printed model enables precise understanding of neurovascular relationships, contributing to safer microsurgical clipping.

title: Anticoagulation Monitoring in Recurrent Venous Thromboembolism Associated With Antiphospholipid Antibodies and Subsequent Heparin-Induced Thrombocytopenia.
abstract: A woman in her 20s with class III obesity and strongly positive antiphospholipid antibodies developed phlegmasia cerulea dolens and a new pulmonary embolus after recent catheter-directed thrombolysis. Before the first documented heparin administration, activated partial thromboplastin time was 95.5 s and international normalized ratio was 1.5. Eight subsequent paired samples showed activated partial thromboplastin times of 176 s to over 200 s with heparin anti-Xa activity of 0.20-0.66 IU/mL. Lupus anticoagulant testing was uninterpretable during anticoagulation, and international normalized ratio reliability was not independently established. Later thrombocytopenia prompted repeat heparin-induced thrombocytopenia testing despite an earlier negative result; a strongly positive immunoassay supported the treating team's diagnosis and transition to fondaparinux. This case illustrates the importance of selecting appropriate anticoagulation monitoring from the outset and reassessing heparin-induced thrombocytopenia when the clinical picture changes. Whether assay interference contributed to recurrent thrombosis remains unresolved.

title: Venous Thromboembolism in Patients Hospitalized With Localized, Regional, and Metastatic Head and Neck Cancer.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) is a known complication in cancer patients, but data in head and neck cancer (HNC)-particularly distinguishing localized, regional, and metastatic disease-are limited. METHODS: Using the 2016-2020 National Inpatient Sample, we examined adults ≥ 18 years with HNC, excluding patients with another primary malignancy. Metastatic status was categorized as localized, regional, and metastatic. Outcomes included odds of VTE, pulmonary embolism (PE), deep vein thrombosis (DVT), inhospital mortality, and prolonged length of stay (LOS ≥ 7 days). Multivariable logistic regression identified factors associated with these outcomes. RESULTS: Among 62 032 unweighted (310 160 weighted) admissions, 75.0% had localized HNC, 12.7% had regional HNC, and 12.3% had metastatic HNC; 2.6% had VTE (2.4% localized HNC, 2.3% regional HNC, and 4.1% metastatic HNC). Compared with localized HNC, regional HNC was not associated with increased odds of VTE, PE, or DVT, whereas metastatic HNC was associated with higher adjusted odds of VTE (aOR 1.52; 95% CI: 1.30-1.78), PE (aOR 1.61; 95% CI: 1.32-1.98), and DVT (aOR 1.47; 95% CI: 1.18-1.83). VTE was associated with increased inhospital mortality (aOR 1.98; 95% CI: 1.64-2.40) and prolonged LOS (aOR 2.14; 95% CI: 1.92-2.39). CONCLUSION: In hospitalized patients, distant, but not regional, metastatic HNC is associated with higher odds of VTE, and VTE is associated with adverse in-hospital outcomes including increased mortality and prolonged LOS.

title: Stenosis of a novel frozen elephant trunk in a patient with chronic dissection.
abstract: A partial elephant trunk (PET), a new type of frozen elephant trunk, was designed to prevent distal stent graft-induced new entry using a thinner nitinol wire with less radial force. We report a case of PET stenosis in chronic dissection. Total arch replacement was performed using a PET. After weaning from cardiopulmonary bypass, the lower-limb blood pressure decreased to 90% of the upper-limb blood pressure. Intraoperative transesophageal echocardiography revealed incomplete PET expansion, and on postoperative day 1, the lower-to-upper body blood pressure ratio further decreased to 70% due to PET stenosis at the steeply angulated arch. Emergency thoracic endovascular aortic repair was successfully performed, completely resolving the pressure gradient.

title: Intravascular Lithotripsy of Aortic and Renal Lesions as a Therapeutic Tool for Pickering Syndrome: A Case Report.
abstract: We report the case of a 73-year-old woman admitted with Pickering syndrome, a life-threatening condition characterized by recurrent flash pulmonary edema secondary to severe renovascular disease. Computed tomography angiography demonstrated an atrophic left kidney, a heavily calcified visceral aorta with a coral-reef morphology, and a near-occlusive stenosis of the right renal artery. Urgent endovascular treatment was performed with intravascular lithotripsy for plaque modification of the suprarenal aorta and the right renal artery, followed by renal artery stenting. The patient showed prompt clinical recovery, with resolution of pulmonary edema, stabilization of blood pressure, and improvement of renal function. This case illustrates the potential role of intravascular lithotripsy as a minimally invasive adjunct for managing severely calcified aorto-renal disease in high-risk patients, enabling endovascular treatment in otherwise challenging anatomy.

title: Transarterial Computed Tomographic Angiography in Patients With Impaired Renal Function Undergoing Endovascular Aortic Repair.
abstract: P PurposeComputed tomography angiography (CTA) is crucial for preoperative planning and postoperative surveillance of endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR). Renal function impairment however limits pre- and postoperative assessment. The aim of our study was to evaluate the safety and diagnostic value of a novel technique in the setting of patients undergoing EVAR.Methods216 patients with chronic kidney disease undergoing transbrachial placement of an angiography catheter in the aorta for contrast medium administration were analyzed retrospectively. 45 patients with normal kidney function and aortic aneurysms were included as control group. 27 were female, 84 cases were for thoracoabdominal aortic aneurysm, while 106 cases were for abdominal aortic aneurysm. Primary endpoint was the freedom from contrast-induced acute kidney injury. Secondary safety endpoints were freedom from access site complications and cerebrovascular incidents. Imaging quality endpoints were attenuation values and contrast-to-noise-ratios in predefined vessels, validated by intraclass correlation coefficients.ResultsMean creatinine change was -.11 mg/dL, mean GFR change was 2.13% in the intervention group. There were 10 (4.6%) false aneurysms and two access site hematoma (0.93%). Two cerebrovascular incidents (0.9%) were transient. Transarterial CTA attenuation values varied between 210.4 (±89) and 241.4 (±98) Hounsfield units (HU), and 306.35 (±63.27) to 321.39 (±70.12) HU in the control group. The mean amount of contrast medium used in the catheter group was significantly reduced (31.70 ± 5.82 mL) compared to the control group (= .001). Contrast-to-noise ratios varied between 9.1 (±4.6) and 11.1 (±4.4. Intraclass correlation coefficients between the readings were very good (0.987-0.992).ConclusionCatheter-based transarterial computed tomographic angiography is a safe and efficacious way to evaluate patients with aortic aneurysms, both prior and after EVAR.

title: Perioperative management of acute type A aortic dissection using extended half-life factor IX (Alprolix) in a patient with severe hemophilia B: a case report.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Emergency surgery for acute type A aortic dissection (ATAAD) in patients with severe hemophilia B is extremely rare, and perioperative coagulation management is a major challenge. CASE PRESENTATION: A 63-year-old man with severe hemophilia B (factor IX activity < 1%) was diagnosed with ATAAD and underwent emergency surgery. Replacement therapy with an extended half-life factor IX product (eftrenonacog alfa; Alprolix) was administered targeting a factor IX activity of 80-100%, and total arch replacement was performed. Cardiopulmonary bypass was performed under standard heparinization conditions. Since rapid measurement of factor IX activity was not possible, postoperative replacement therapy was based primarily on the clinical assessment of hemostasis, with serial activated partial thromboplastin time measurements providing supportive information, whereas intraoperative anticoagulation was managed using standard activated clotting time monitoring. Intra- and postoperative bleeding volumes were within ranges comparable to those observed in standard complex aortic surgery, and the postoperative course was uneventful. CONCLUSIONS: The use of an extended half-life factor IX product may be a practical option for perioperative coagulation management during emergency aortic surgery in patients with severe hemophilia B.

title: Integrative genetic analyses for drug repurposing identify emodin as a candidate modulator of STAT3 signaling in abdominal aortic aneurysm.
abstract: Abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) is a life-threatening vascular disease lacking effective pharmacological therapies. To identify potential therapeutic targets and candidate compounds, we performed integrative genetic analyses for drug repurposing by combining Mendelian randomization (MR), summary-data-based Mendelian randomization (SMR), and Bayesian colocalization. This framework prioritized multiple druggable candidates, among which STAT3 emerged as a key regulatory node. Subsequent functional studies demonstrated that emodin suppressed vascular smooth muscle cell proliferation, migration, phenotypic switching, and inflammatory responses. These effects were accompanied by reduced STAT3 phosphorylation and nuclear localization. Molecular docking suggested a potential binding mode of emodin within the STAT3 SH2 domain, while cellular thermal shift assays demonstrated thermal stabilization of STAT3 by emodin in intact cells, consistent with target engagement. Notably, emodin and the selective STAT3 inhibitor STAT3-IN-13 produced comparable effects, and co-treatment did not yield additive efficacy, suggesting overlapping mechanisms. In vivo, emodin attenuated aneurysm development and reduced vascular inflammation in experimental models. Collectively, these findings identify emodin as a candidate modulator of AAA progression acting through suppression of STAT3-associated signaling pathways, and demonstrate the potential of genetic evidence-guided drug repurposing strategies in complex vascular diseases.
englishSummary: Abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) is a life-threatening vascular disease lacking effective pharmacological therapies. To identify potential therapeutic targets and candidate compounds, we performed integrative genetic analyses for drug repurposing by combining Mendelian randomization (MR), summary-data-based Mendelian randomization (SMR), and Bayesian colocalization. This framework prioritized multiple druggable candidates, among which STAT3 emerged as a key regulatory node.

title: Early and follow-up results of reinterventions for type 2 endoleak following endovascular repair of abdominal aortic aneurysm (EVAR): the multicenter REinterventions for Type 2 Endoleak (RETE) study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Type II endoleak (T2EL) is frequent after endovascular abdominal aortic aneurysm repair (EVAR) and may require reintervention in selected patients. However, the optimal treatment strategy for durable resolution remains uncertain. The aim of this study is to retrospectively analyze perioperative and long-term results of T2Els' reinterventions, both endovascular and open surgical, in a large patient cohort from twenty high-volume academic centers. METHODS: A retrospective analysis of consecutive patients undergoing first reintervention for T2ELs was conducted across 20 centers over a 10-year period. Patients requiring concomitant treatment for other endoleak types were excluded. A total of 403 patients were included. Primary outcomes included technical success, 30-day AAA-related mortality and reintervention-free survival during follow-up. Secondary outcomes were perioperative complications, early reintervention, overall survival, freedom from aneurysm-related death and rupture, freedom from recurrent endoleaks, freedom from open conversion or semi-conversion in patients previously treated endovascularly and sac behavior during follow-up. Kaplan-Meier curves and Cox regression analyses were performed to analyze follow-up results. RESULTS: Patients were predominantly male (90%) with a mean age of 77 years. Reintervention was indicated for sac enlargement in 94.5% of cases; 4% presented with rupture. Median time from EVAR to reintervention was 4.3 years. Lumbar arteries (55%) and the inferior mesenteric artery (35%) were the main sources. Endovascular treatment was performed in 86% and open conversion/semi-conversion in 14%. Technical success was 96%, with 1% mortality and 4% major complications. Overall survival was 80.5% and rupture-free survival 79.2% at 5 years. Recurrent T2EL occurred in 64.2%, and reintervention-free survival was 48.3%. Endovascular group showed significantly lower freedom from reintervention rates when compared to open conversion/semi conversion group (42.4% vs 86.8%, SE 0.04 vs SE 0.05, p<0.001, log-rank 15.9). Conversion/semi-conversion after endovascular treatment occurred in 14%. No differences were recorded comparing different fabric materials of the endograft in terms of freedom for reintervention and freedom from open surgery. A sac diameter ≥7 cm at the time of reintervention predicted further reinterventions, while primary open treatment improved durability. CONCLUSIONS: Reinterventions for T2ELs are safe, with satisfactory immediate technical success and low perioperative mortality. During follow-up, risks of rupture and AAA-related death remain low. However, the endoleak recurrence rate exceeds 60% at five years, necessitating reintervention in over 40% of patients. Early intervention for patients with a sac diameter approaching 7 cm can be suggested, while a primary open approach may be considered in low-risk patients.

However, the optimal treatment strategy for durable resolution remains uncertain. The aim of this study is to retrospectively analyze perioperative and long-term results of T2Els' reinterventions, both endovascular and open surgical, in a large patient cohort from twenty high-volume academic centers.

title: Risk Factors and Clinical Outcomes of Reocclusion after Endovascular Treatment for Acute Ischemic Stroke: An Updated Systematic Review, Meta-Analysis and Meta-Regression.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Early reocclusion after endovascular treatment (EVT) for acute ischemic stroke is underrecognized; its determinants and impact remain poorly defined. METHODS: Random-effects meta-analysis of early reocclusion after successful EVT (PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library through January 2026). Crude odds ratios (ORs) were pooled and certainty rated with GRADE. Post hoc sensitivity analyses included only same-site reocclusion definitions. RESULTS: Ten studies (3,381 patients) were included; 244 (7.2%) reoccluded. Reocclusion was associated with lower 90-day functional independence (OR 0.25, 95% CI 0.17-0.38) and higher mortality (OR 1.86, 1.29-2.68), both moderate certainty. Reocclusion was more frequent with large-artery atherosclerosis (OR 2.24, 1.41-3.55; same-site 3.04, 1.73-5.33) and less frequent with cardioembolism (OR 0.40, 0.28-0.57) and atrial fibrillation (OR 0.39, 0.26-0.59), mutually confounded associations reflecting one embolic-versus-atherothrombotic axis. Prestroke antiplatelet therapy (OR 0.43, 0.28-0.67) lost significance under the same-site definition (0.60, 0.31-1.16). Exploratory data (two cohorts) linked eTICI 2c-3 reperfusion with less reocclusion (OR 0.44, 0.28-0.69). No study reported when etiology was adjudicated; the atherosclerosis association may be partly outcome-induced. CONCLUSIONS: Early reocclusion is uncommon but carries a substantial prognostic penalty. Its determinants appear to lie in the vascular substrate rather than thrombectomy technique; prospective studies with uniform same-site definitions and systematic follow-up imaging are needed.

METHODS: Random-effects meta-analysis of early reocclusion after successful EVT (PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library through January 2026). Crude odds ratios (ORs) were pooled and certainty rated with GRADE.

title: Does the HPB surgeon need a vascular surgeon?
abstract: Complex HPB surgery increasingly requires vascular resection and reconstruction. Therefore, vascular expertise is an essential part of surgical planning, technical execution, and oncological decision-making. While highly complex arterial, caval, or ex situ procedures should remain concentrated in specialised centres, every HPB surgeon should possess core vascular competence. Vascular and transplantation training should therefore become an integral part of advanced HPB education.

title: Effect of Extended-Duration Venous Thromboprophylaxis After Cancer Surgery.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Cancer patients undergoing surgery are at significantly increased risk of venous thromboembolism (VTE). Although extended thromboprophylaxis is recommended, the optimal anticoagulant type and duration remain unclear. This study aimed to evaluate the comparative efficacy and safety of different extended thromboprophylaxis in this population. METHODS: A Bayesian network meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) was performed to evaluate various thromboprophylaxis strategies for patients undergoing cancer-related surgery. We conducted both three-node and five-node network analyses to evaluate extended-duration versus standard-duration thromboprophylaxis strategies. Outcomes included venous thromboembolism, major bleeding, and all-cause mortality. Net clinical benefit and risk-benefit assessments were additionally performed to determine the overall impact of prolonged anticoagulant therapy. Treatment effects were summarized as risk ratios (RRs) with corresponding 95% credible intervals (CrIs). RESULTS: A total of 14 randomized controlled trials involving 4,331 participants were included. Compared with placebo, extended-duration prophylaxis with direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) (RR 0.12, 95% CrI 0.05-0.27) and low-molecular-weight heparin (LMWH) (RR 0.17, 95% CrI 0.05-0.55) significantly reduced the incidence of venous thromboembolism without a corresponding increase in major bleeding. In net clinical benefit analyses, both prolonged DOAC therapy (RR 0.27, 95% CrI 0.14-0.49) and LMWH (RR 0.36, 95% CrI 0.17-0.76) demonstrated favorable overall outcomes. Risk-benefit evaluation suggested that prolonged DOACs provided a more advantageous balance than LMWH, with an NNH/NNT ratio of 4.17. CONCLUSIONS: Extended thromboprophylaxis is effective and safe for cancer patients undergoing surgery. Besides, DOACs appears to be the optimal anticoagulant for extended thromboprophylaxis, providing the greatest net clinical benefit.

Although extended thromboprophylaxis is recommended, the optimal anticoagulant type and duration remain unclear. This study aimed to evaluate the comparative efficacy and safety of different extended thromboprophylaxis in this population.

title: Computer tomography imaging for suspected acute aortic syndrome.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Acute Aortic Syndrome (AAS) is a life-threatening condition that presents diagnostic challenges due to variable clinical presentations. Limited data exists regarding Computed Tomography Angiography (CTA) utilisation patterns and outcomes for patients with suspected AAS in Irish emergency departments (ED). This study evaluates trends in CTA utilisation and positivity rate for patients with suspected AAS presenting to a level 4 hospital ED. METHODS: A retrospective single-centre chart review was conducted of all adult patients (≥ 16 years) who underwent CTA aorta imaging requested by emergency medicine physicians in Tallaght University Hospital between January 2018 and December 2025. Patient demographics, imaging findings, time metrics, disposition and mortality were analysed. RESULTS: Among 457,735 ED attendances, 797 eligible CTA aorta studies were performed. There was a 2.86 fold increase in CTA scans done across the study period from 37 studies in 2018 to 106 in 2025. Overall positivity rate for AAS was 2.76% (n = 22). Acute aortic dissection accounted for 77% of positive cases (n = 17), followed by penetrating atherosclerotic ulcers (n = 3) and intramural hematomas (n = 2). Overall mortality among patients with confirmed AAS was 27.27%. CONCLUSION: This study highlights the low positivity rate of CTA aorta scans in an Irish ED but high mortality of patients diagnosed with acute aortic syndrome. Increasing CTA utilisation, alongside the overall low incidence of AAS, suggests opportunities to improve diagnostic efficiency.

title: An enlarged nonfistulous artery mimicking an additional feeder in a pediatric pial arteriovenous fistula: an angiographic pitfall.
abstract: Pial arteriovenous fistulas (PAVFs) are rare high-flow vascular lesions requiring precise characterization of the fistulous angioarchitecture before treatment. We report a pediatric PAVF in which an enlarged artery adjacent to the fistula initially appeared suspicious for additional fistulous supply. Superselective angiography demonstrated normal cortical arterial arborization and parenchymal perfusion without early venous drainage, confirming that the enlarged vessel did not participate directly in the arteriovenous shunt. Selective coil embolization achieved complete immediate occlusion of the fistulous communication while preserving the adjacent normal cortical arterial supply. This case illustrates that arterial enlargement alone does not establish participation in a PAVF and highlights an angiographic pitfall relevant to treatment planning.

title: Characterizing the Thrombotic Spectrum and Clinical Phenotypes of Tranexamic Acid-Associated Adverse Events: A Pharmacovigilance Study Based on the FAERS Database.
abstract: Tranexamic acid (TXA) is widely used to reduce bleeding in surgical, trauma, obstetric, and gynecological settings. However, concerns remain regarding TXA-associated thrombotic adverse events, and their phenotypic heterogeneity and clinical severity have not been comprehensively characterized. This study investigated TXA-associated thrombotic events using the Food and Drug Administration Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS) from 2004Q1 to 2026Q1. Thrombotic adverse events were identified using the Standardized MedDRA Query (SMQ) "Embolic and thrombotic events" and evaluated by disproportionality analysis based on reporting odds ratios (RORs). Qualifying thrombotic events were assigned to the SMQ vessel-type subgroups-arterial, vessel-type unspecified/mixed, and venous-and demographic characteristics, indications, clinical outcomes and time-to-onset were compared across subgroups; signal strength was further related to clinical severity. In all, 515 thrombotic cases associated with TXA and 26 selected thrombotic terms were found (arterial, 157; mixed, 168; venous, 190). Venous thromboembolism-pulmonary embolism (n = 128, ROR 13.94) and deep vein thrombosis (n = 58, ROR 9.09)-is the most frequent type and brings about the most severe and fatal consequences (death reported in 16.8% of venous versus 2.5% of arterial reports), whereas the strongest disproportionality signals were observed for rare site-specific events such as ovarian vein thrombosis (ROR 352.95) and cerebral venous sinus thrombosis (ROR 118.35). The three subgroups differed markedly in demographic and clinical characteristics: venous events occurred predominantly in women (73.7%) treated for menorrhagia (35.3%), whereas arterial events arose mainly in surgical or procedural settings (intravenous route 36.3%; surgery/prophylaxis 19.1%) and presented earliest after exposure [median time-to-onset (TTO) 0 versus 7 days]. Signal strength was not concordant with clinical severity across the thrombotic spectrum. These findings provide a deeper understanding of the thrombotic safety of TXA, indicate that the clinical background may influence the phenotypic differences among the different thrombotic types, and emphasize the necessity of enhanced attention and risk stratification in high-risk groups.

title: Association between thyroid feedback quantile-based index and the risk of in-hospital amputation in patients with diabetic foot ulcer.
abstract: AIMS: To investigate the relationship between the thyroid feedback quantile-based index (TFQI) and the risk of amputation during hospitalization in patients with diabetic foot ulcers (DFU). METHODS: This single-center retrospective study included 381 hospitalized patients with DFU and normal thyroid function. Logistic regression assessed continuous TFQI and quartiles. Model 1 was unadjusted; Model 2 adjusted for age, sex, BMI, and smoking; Model 3 additionally adjusted for diabetes duration, HbA1c, diabetic peripheral neuropathy, peripheral arterial disease, hypertension, CRP, and dyslipidemia. RCS assessed dose-response patterns; Firth regression was used for sensitivity analysis. RESULTS: Fifty-six patients underwent amputation. In Model 3, each 1-SD increase in TFQI (equivalent to a 1-unit increase in pre-scaled TFQI) was associated with higher odds of amputation (OR 2.27, 95% CI 1.63-3.15; P < 0.001). Compared with Q1, ORs were 2.94 (0.98-8.83; P = 0.055), 5.60 (1.88-16.67; P = 0.002), and 14.79 (5.22-41.89; P < 0.001) for Q2, Q3, and Q4, respectively. RCS showed an overall association (P = 0.002) and nonlinearity (P = 0.046) in Model 3. Firth estimates were broadly consistent with conventional regression. CONCLUSION: Among hospitalized DFU patients with normal thyroid function, higher TFQI levels are associated with an increased risk of amputation during hospitalization. Nevertheless, the clinical utility of TFQI requires further validation in prospective studies.

METHODS: This single-center retrospective study included 381 hospitalized patients with DFU and normal thyroid function. Logistic regression assessed continuous TFQI and quartiles.

title: Percutaneous and Endovascular Embolization-Based Treatments of Type 1A and Type 1B Endoleaks after Endovascular Aneurysm Repair.
abstract: ObjectiveThis retrospective, observational study was conducted to evaluate the efficacy of embolization-based treatments for Types 1A and 1B endoleaks following endovascular aneurysm repair.DesignA total of 26 patients who underwent endovascular aneurysm repair between January 2005 and September 2023 and subsequently received embolization therapy for Types 1A or 1B endoleak, either at the end of the procedure or during follow-up, were retrospectively reviewed.MethodsEmbolization was performed in 16 patients with Type 1A endoleaks and 10 with Type 1B. Eight of the 16 patients who underwent embolization for Type 1A endoleaks required additional treatments such as aortic cuff placement or a chimney graft. Similarly, six out of the 10 patients treated with embolization for Type 1B endoleaks underwent adjunctive procedures such as iliac stent-graft extension. The primary endpoint was the absence of aneurysm sac enlargement. Secondary endpoints included technical success and the avoidance of endoleak-related reintervention.ResultsAneurysm sac regression or stabilization was observed in 68.7% of Type 1A and 70% of Type 1B endoleak cases over mean follow-up periods of 43.1 and 22.3 months, respectively.ConclusionEmbolization-based endovascular treatment, alone or combined with adjunctive endograft procedures, may achieve aneurysm sac stabilization or regression in a substantial proportion of patients with Types 1A and 1B endoleaks. However, the possibility of recurrence and reintervention, particularly in Type 1A endoleaks, remains an important limitation of this approach and warrants continued imaging surveillance.

title: EXPRESS: Cerebral blood flow-oxygen metabolism uncoupling at 24 hours after stroke thrombectomy.
abstract: BackgroundFollowing successful endovascular therapy (EVT) for acute ischemic stroke, tissue with abnormal perfusion may have impaired oxygen extraction and metabolism. MRI model-based oxygen extraction fraction (OEFmax) and cerebral metabolic rate of oxygen (CMRO2) were characterized in hypoperfusion and hyperemia regions 24 hours post-EVT.MethodsEighty-four patients were included with anterior circulation vessel occlusion, successful recanalization, and an MRI at 24 hours post-EVT. Time-to-maximum (Tmax) and cerebral blood flow (CBF) were evaluated for hypoperfusion and hyperemia. CBF, OEFmax, and CMRO2 were quantified using i) segmentation-based and ii) single slice region of interest (ROI) analyses. Normalized CBF, OEFmax, and CMRO2 were calculated by dividing the segmentation or ROI value by the contralateral value.ResultsSixty-seven (80%) patients had abnormal perfusion; hypoperfusion in 22 (26%), hyperemia in 36 (43%), and both in 9 (11%). Compared to control, hypoperfused regions demonstrated a 62% CBF decrease, 52% CMRO2 decrease, and 68% OEFmax increase (p<0.01). Hyperemic regions demonstrated a 58% CBF increase, 26% CMRO2 increase, and 25% OEFmax decrease (p<0.01). Hyperemia had no significant correlation between normalized CBF and CMRO2 (p=0.14).ConclusionHyperemia regions demonstrated cerebral blood flow-oxygen metabolism uncoupling, suggesting the underlying mechanism as loss of cerebrovascular autoregulation rather than hypermetabolic demand.

title: Venous sinus of Kelch: a cadaveric study with embryological insights and clinical implications.
abstract: The venous sinus of Kelch (VSK) represents a rare but clinically significant venous variant of the middle cranial fossa, with very limited documentation in the existing literature. This study aimed to understand the morphology, course, and morphometry of VSK along with associated variations in the drainage pattern of the superficial middle cerebral vein (SMCV) and middle meningeal sinus (MMS). This study was conducted over the period from 2022 to 2025 at Zoram Medical College and Hospital, Aizawl, Mizoram. In the present study, VSK was observed in 9.26% of the 54 middle cranial fossae examined from 27 cadavers. Moreover, SMCV and MMS, which normally drain into either the spheno-parietal sinus or cavernous sinus, drained into VSK. From an embryological perspective, VSK can be understood as a persistent primitive tentorial sinus (PTS). The variable course and termination of PTS may also result in other reported venous variants like Spheno-basal sinus, Spheno-petrosal sinus and Petro-basal sinus, which underscore the complexity of venous adaptations influenced by hemodynamic factors. Clinically, awareness of such variants is crucial for accurate radiological interpretation and for minimising the risk of iatrogenic injury during surgical and endovascular procedures involving the middle cranial fossa. Importantly, recognition of these alternative venous pathways may have future implications in facilitating novel endovascular approaches for neuromodulation, targeted therapy, and minimally invasive access to the temporal lobe and trigeminal nerve.
englishSummary: The venous sinus of Kelch (VSK) represents a rare but clinically significant venous variant of the middle cranial fossa, with very limited documentation in the existing literature. This study aimed to understand the morphology, course, and morphometry of VSK along with associated variations in the drainage pattern of the superficial middle cerebral vein (SMCV) and middle meningeal sinus (MMS). This study was conducted over the period from 2022 to 2025 at Zoram Medical College and Hospital, Aizawl, Mizoram.

title: Use of vaginal estrogens in urogynecology: current evidence, controversies and clinical applications.
abstract: PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Genitourinary syndrome of menopause (GSM) is a prevalent yet underrecognized condition in postmenopausal women, characterized by progressive vulvovaginal and lower urinary tract symptoms from estrogen deficiency. Vaginal estrogen therapy is the first-line pharmacologic treatment for GSM. However, as new evidence emerges, understanding of its efficacy, safety, and use in special populations continues to evolve. This review summarizes current evidence on vaginal estrogen formulations, clinical effectiveness, safety, and therapeutic applications. RECENT FINDINGS: Recent randomized controlled trials confirm that low-dose vaginal estrogen significantly improves GSM symptoms - including vaginal dryness, dyspareunia, and irritation - while restoring epithelial integrity and normalizing pH. Evidence also supports its role in reducing recurrent urinary tract infections by restoring lactobacilli-dominant flora, reinforced by a 2025 multisociety clinical guideline recommending topical, but not systemic, estrogen for this indication. Comparative studies show similar efficacy across creams, tablets, inserts, and rings, differing primarily in convenience and absorption rather than effectiveness. Large cohort studies indicate no increased risk of cardiovascular disease, venous thromboembolism, or malignancy. Use in breast cancer survivors remains controversial, but emerging data suggest minimal systemic absorption and no clear increase in recurrence risk, supporting shared decision-making. In addition, long-term outcomes show that adjunctive vaginal estrogen does not improve anatomic surgical success after native tissue apical prolapse repair. Nonhormonal therapies and agents like ospemifene or prasterone offer alternative options, though they demonstrate lower or more variable efficacy than vaginal estrogen. SUMMARY: Vaginal estrogen therapy is the most effective, evidence-based treatment for GSM and helps prevent recurrent urinary tract infections in postmenopausal women. Its favorable safety profile and multiple formulations enable individualized care. Recent evidence clarifies that while overall safety is reassuring, caution is necessary for breast cancer survivors using aromatase inhibitors. Additionally, longer-term perioperative trial data temper expectations regarding surgical-recurrence benefits, while confirming its value for local tissue optimization. Ongoing research should focus on long-term safety in high-risk groups and the effectiveness of emerging non-estrogen alternatives.

However, as new evidence emerges, understanding of its efficacy, safety, and use in special populations continues to evolve.

title: Arabidopsis Loss of tRNA uridine thiolation affects mRNA translation, protein production, and metabolite accumulation in.
abstract: Arabidopsis thaliana 34 It is well established in yeast and animal system that the level of uridine thiolation at position 34 of tRNA anticodon loops can impact the decoding potential of the corresponding codons. Using, we confirm that the ability of the plant ribosome to decode AAA, GAA, and CAA codons is impaired when this thiol group is lost, leading to a reduction in protein production, especially for genes enriched in these codons. Interestingly, we observed that loss of tRNA thiolation results in variations in the levels of numerous proteins involved in sulfur-compound metabolism and amino acid biosynthesis. These variations, in turn, affect the accumulation of several sulfur-containing metabolites and amino acids, suggesting that the level of tRNA thiolation has a direct and profound impact on plant metabolism. We also demonstrate that Uthiolation is essential for adjusting plant growth in response to sulfur limitation and that its absence directly affects the plant's interaction with bacteria, including both pathogens and beneficial organisms. Our results support the hypothesis that the level of tRNA thiolation can be used in plant to link nutritional status to translation.

title: Contemporary Analysis of the Volume-Outcome Relationship for Patients With Nontraumatic Subarachnoid Hemorrhage.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Nontraumatic subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH) carries a substantial mortality burden and risk of long-term morbidity. Although prior investigations have demonstrated an inverse association between SAH admission volume and in-hospital mortality, reported thresholds remain broad. Importantly, the relative importance of both admission and procedural volume has yet to be evaluated on a national scale. We examined the association of volume metrics with outcomes in an SAH cohort. METHODS: All adult (≥18 years) hospitalizations with a primary diagnosis of nontraumatic SAH were identified from the 2016 to 2022 Nationwide Readmissions Database. Multivariable regression models were developed to evaluate the independent and joint associations of SAH admission and clipping and coiling procedural volume with in-hospital outcomes. RESULTS: P P Of an estimated 142 271 hospitalizations, index mortality was 20.2%. Following risk adjustment, both increasing SAH admission volume and clipping and coiling procedural volume were independently associated with reduced mortality. When modeled jointly, however, clipping and coiling procedural volume remained an independent predictor of mortality (adjusted odds ratio, 0.981 per 10 procedures,<0.001) whereas SAH admission volume was no longer significant (=0.40). CONCLUSIONS: Joint examination of SAH and clipping and coiling procedural volume revealed procedural caseload to be the dominant predictor of in-hospital mortality, suggesting that survival benefits historically attributed to admission volume may be more precisely explained by procedural expertise. These findings support reexamination of volume-based benchmarks in contemporary cerebrovascular care frameworks.

title: Dapagliflozin After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation According to Frailty in DapaTAVI Trial.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Frailty is common in patients with severe aortic stenosis undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation and portends worse outcomes. Whether the benefit of posttranscatheter aortic valve implantation dapagliflozin differs by frailty is uncertain. METHODS: In this post hoc analysis, we investigated the efficacy of dapagliflozin according to frailty status in the DapaTAVI (Dapagliflozin in Patients Undergoing Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation) trial. Frailty was assessed through the Fatigue, Resistance, Ambulation, Illnesses, and Loss of Weight scale (robust=0, prefrail=1-2, frail=3-5). The primary outcome was the composite of all-cause death or worsening heart failure at 1 year. RESULTS: P P Among 1222 patients with baseline frailty assessment, 47.2% were frail, 40.3% prefrail, and 12.4% robust. Over 12 months, 215 patients (17.6%) experienced the primary end point. Patients who were prefrail and frail had higher risk than robust patients (adjusted hazard ratios [HRs], 1.88 [95% CI, 1.05-3.38] and 2.29 [1.29-4.07], respectively;=0.004). Dapagliflozin was associated with a lower risk of the primary end point in patients who were frail (HR, 0.53 [95% CI, 0.36-0.77]) but not in those who were prefrail (HR, 1.01 [95% CI, 0.66-1.55]) or robust patients (HR, 1.26 [95% CI, 0.42-3.75]);for interaction=0.021. There was no evidence that frailty modified the safety profile of dapagliflozin. CONCLUSIONS: Frailty was common and independently associated with worse outcomes after transcatheter aortic valve implantation. Dapagliflozin appeared to confer greater relative benefit in patients with frailty.

title: Exercise and Thoracic Aortic Aneurysms: A Paradigm Shift Toward Informed, Personalized Activity Guidelines.
abstract: Exercise is widely recognized for its cardiovascular benefits; however, its safety and role in patients with thoracic aortic aneurysms (TAAs) remains complex due to its distinctive biomechanical vulnerabilities. Fundamentally different from abdominal aortic aneurysms, TAAs develop from distinct pathophysiological processes that affect their hemodynamic responses to stressors and influence their risk of adverse aortic events. Exercise induces acute hemodynamic changes, including increased stroke volume, systolic and pulse pressures, and transient aortic stiffening. These changes impose mechanical stress on the aortic wall, potentially accelerating aneurysm progression or triggering adverse aortic events. Although moderate aerobic exercise generally appears safe with potential cardiovascular benefits, evidence supporting safe practices in TAAs is limited. Current guidelines frequently extrapolate from abdominal aortic aneurysm data, which overlook the specificities of the thoracic aorta. This review underscores the urgent need for comprehensive research, using advanced imaging, biomarker profiling, and real-time hemodynamic monitoring to understand how different exercise modalities and intensities affect TAAs. Well-designed prospective studies are crucial to improve risk stratification, optimize antihypertensive strategies, develop personalized exercise prescriptions, and provide evidence-informed guidance to patients. Perioperative strategies like prehabilitation and structured postoperative rehabilitation show promise but lack rigorous evaluation. Ultimately, this work advocates a paradigm shift from conservative inactivity toward informed, individualized physical activity regimens tailored to each patient's risk profile. This approach aims to maximize cardiovascular benefits while minimizing adverse aortic events, thereby improving overall health and quality of life in patients with TAAs.

title: Paradoxical Association of Body Mass Index With Occurrence and Mortality of Venous Thromboembolism in Hospitalized Patients: A National Hospital-Based Cohort Analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The association between body mass index (BMI) and venous thromboembolism (VTE) occurrence and mortality is controversial. This study aimed to investigate the association of BMI with VTE occurrence and mortality and explore the consistency across age, sex, and medical specialty. METHODS: 2 2 2 2 This study included 3 199 526 inpatients at potential risk for VTE from a nationwide hospital-based cohort. Participants were categorized as lean weight (BMI <18.5 kg/m), normal weight (18.5 ≤BMI<24.0 kg/m), overweight (24.0 ≤BMI <28.0 kg/m), and obesity (BMI ≥28.0 kg/m). Odds ratios (ORs) were calculated by logistic regression models. RESULTS: P P for interaction for interaction In all participants, 59 002 (1.8%) developed VTE during hospitalization. After adjusting for the confounding factors, compared with normal weight, the risk of VTE occurrence reduced by 18% (odds ratio [OR], 0.82 [95% CI, 0.80-0.83]) in participants with overweight and 22% (OR, 0.78,[95% CI, 0.75-0.81]) in participants with obesity. The protective association of overweight/obesity was more pronounced in age ≥65 years, female patients, and surgery participants (<0.05), whereas in internal medical participants, obesity was associated with a higher risk of VTE occurrence (OR, 1.11 [95% CI, 1.01-1.21]). A total of 636 (1.1%) patients with VTE died before discharge. No significant association was observed between overweight/obesity and post-VTE mortality. However, in the surgical subgroup, obesity was associated with a lower risk of post-VTE mortality (OR, 0.37 [95% CI, 0.17-0.80],<0.05). CONCLUSION: An inverse association between BMI and VTE occurrence was observed among at-risk inpatients, most pronounced in older, female, and surgical subgroups. Notably, obesity remained a risk factor in medical patients, whereas among surgical patients who developed VTE, it was paradoxically associated with lower mortality.

title: Ultralow-contrast stepping digital subtraction angiography for whole-limb arterial evaluation: A case report.
abstract: Stepping digital subtraction angiography (DSA) enables whole-limb arterial assessment with a single contrast injection, and diluted contrast medium may further reduce iodine exposure. A patient in their 80s with an abdominal aortic aneurysm and bilateral common iliac artery aneurysms was scheduled for staged internal iliac artery embolization before endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR). Due to a mural thrombus in the left common iliac artery aneurysm, right internal iliac artery embolization was performed via an ipsilateral approach. Severe right external iliac artery stenosis prompted stepping DSA before and after embolization to evaluate distal embolization. Sevenfold- and tenfold-diluted stepping DSA examinations were performed before and after embolization, respectively, using identical injection parameters (3 mL/s; 30 mL). These required 4.29 and 3.0 mL of undiluted contrast medium, respectively. Although pedal artery enhancement was reduced with tenfold dilution, image quality remained acceptable, and no obvious distal embolization was identified in the visualized arteries; however, small emboli in poorly opacified pedal branches could not be excluded with tenfold dilution. Because internal iliac artery embolization was not expected to significantly alter lower-extremity arterial perfusion, the observed difference in image quality was considered to primarily reflect the difference between the two dilution protocols rather than changes in arterial hemodynamics. Ultralow-contrast stepping DSA may be a contrast-saving technique in selected cases when repeated whole-limb arterial evaluation is required.

A patient in their 80s with an abdominal aortic aneurysm and bilateral common iliac artery aneurysms was scheduled for staged internal iliac artery embolization before endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR). Due to a mural thrombus in the left common iliac artery aneurysm, right internal iliac artery embolization was performed via an ipsilateral approach.

title: Delayed deterioration after surgical treatment of a spinal dural arteriovenous fistula detected by three spinal angiographies: Case report.
abstract: Spinal dural arteriovenous fistulas (DAVFs) are the most common subtype of spinal arteriovenous malformations, and they often cause progressive myelopathy. Early detection and intervention are critical to preventing irreversible neurological deficits. Selective spinal angiography remains the gold standard for diagnosing this condition. However, for some patients with typical clinical features and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) findings consistent with DAVF, the initial angiography may fail to detect the lesion. In this article, we report a case of T4 low-flow spinal DAVF that was only identified after three rounds of spinal angiography. The fistula was successfully occluded via surgery, and the patient's symptoms gradually improved postoperatively. Nevertheless, the patient later developed recurrent, aggravated symptoms. The delayed deterioration of previously resolved symptoms was attributed to venous thrombosis, and the condition improved after systemic anticoagulation therapy with heparin. The patients fluctuating symptoms stabilized one month after combined therapy with anticoagulants and antiplatelet drugs. For patients with a high clinical suspicion of spinal DAVF, required to confirm the final diagnosis. Delayed deterioration can occur secondary to progressive venous thrombosis, so preventive anticoagulation is indicated for selected patient's, and this intervention should be individualized.

title: Retinal Microvascular Abnormalities, White Matter Injury, and Cognitive Impairment in Carotid Stenosis or Occlusion.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Severe carotid artery stenosis or occlusion (CASO) is associated with white matter injury and cognitive impairment, but markers of accompanying microvascular dysfunction remain incompletely characterized. We investigated the relationships among retinal microvascular abnormalities on optical coherence tomography angiography, white matter hyperintensities (WMH), and cognitive impairment in severe unilateral CASO. METHODS: In this multicenter cross-sectional study, 860 participants were included: 566 patients with severe unilateral CASO without acute cerebral infarction and 294 control participants with similar age and sex distributions. All participants underwent multimodal imaging, including automated WMH segmentation on brain magnetic resonance imaging and macular optical coherence tomography angiography. Cognitive function was assessed using the Montreal Cognitive Assessment. RESULTS: P Compared with controls, patients with CASO showed lower vessel length density across retinal layers and greater WMH burden. Within the group with CASO, the retina ipsilateral to the stenosis showed lower vessel length density and greater vessel dilation, paralleling the greater burden of deep WMH in the ipsilateral hemisphere (all adjusted<0.05). Retinal microvascular abnormalities and greater WMH burden were both associated with worse concurrent cognitive performance. Adding optical coherence tomography angiography metrics to clinical and WMH-based models provided modest additional discrimination for identifying concurrent cognitive impairment in internal cross-validation, increasing the area under the curve from 0.652 to 0.695 (Δarea under the curve, 0.043 [95% CI, 0.021-0.064]). CONCLUSIONS: In severe unilateral CASO, retinal microvascular abnormalities were associated with ipsilateral white matter injury and lower cognitive performance. Optical coherence tomography angiographymetrics provided modest complementary discriminatory information beyond conventional clinical variables and WMH for identifying concurrent cognitive impairment, although external validation is required. title: How far are vision-free medical robots from achieving trustworthy embodied intelligence?
abstract: Embodied Intelligence (EI) is rapidly reshaping the field of robotic surgery, enabling unprecedented levels of clinical precision while liberating surgeons from excessive cognitive and physical burdens. However, for "vision-free" surgical robots incapable of integrating direct visual sensing-such as endovascular robots and untethered swarms-their persistent reliance on external medical imaging fundamentally impedes their evolution toward safe and trustworthy EI-surgery.

title: Streamlined 2D multimodal fusion framework predicts 90 day functional outcomes in acute ischemic stroke.
abstract: Functional outcome prediction after endovascular therapy can support early risk stratification in acute ischemic stroke. We developed a 2D multimodal fusion framework using multicenter data from 405 patients with post-interventional cerebral hyperdensity on immediate non-contrast CT. Radiomic and deep transfer learning features were extracted from the single CT slice showing the largest hyperdensity area and combined with clinical variables using an Extra Trees classifier. In the external test cohort, the fusion model predicted unfavorable 90-day outcome, defined as a modified Rankin Scale score greater than 2, with an AUC of 0.803, specificity of 88.0%, positive predictive value of 93.3%, and sensitivity of 60.9%. SHAP analysis identified malignant cerebral edema, age, baseline NIHSS, reperfusion status, and imaging intensity descriptors as influential factors. By reducing dependence on 3D segmentation, this framework provides an early phase (within 5 days) prognostic assessment tool for individualized in-hospital risk stratification after thrombectomy.

title: Duplex ultrasound as an initial imaging clue to spontaneous isolated celiac artery dissection: A case report.
abstract: Spontaneous isolated celiac artery dissection is uncommon and is usually confirmed with computed tomography angiography (CTA). Duplex ultrasound may provide an initial clue when the lesion and its flow abnormalities are directly visualized. A 56-year-old woman with untreated hypertension presented with acute persistent epigastric pain radiating to the back. Color Doppler ultrasound at the celiac artery origin demonstrated an intimal flap separating the true and false lumens, with an adjacent hypoechoic component without detectable flow. Spectral Doppler sampling within the dissected segment showed a peak systolic velocity of 225 cm/s with spectral broadening. Initial CTA confirmed proximal celiac artery dissection. On short-interval repeat imaging, the maximum outer diameter at the same anatomic level increased from 8.8 mm to 9.7 mm, the true lumen became more compressed, and new false-lumen thrombosis appeared. Symptoms had not progressed; the decision to intervene was driven by imaging progression. False-lumen coil embolization and stent placement were performed. Follow-up CTA demonstrated a patent stent, preserved major branch perfusion, and no residual false-lumen opacification. In this patient, duplex ultrasound provided an initial imaging clue, whereas CTA confirmed the diagnosis, documented interval remodeling, and assessed the post-treatment anatomy.

title: [Primary and secondary microsurgical reconstruction in soft tissue sarcomas].
abstract: The reconstruction after soft tissue sarcoma resection is sometimes essential to enable radical R0 resection, limb salvage, satisfactory functional outcomes and timely adjuvant treatment. In a retrospective cohort of 76 soft tissue reconstructions of the lower limbs, predominantly following external resections, wound coverage was consistently performed in a staged manner with a mean interval of 18 days; in more than half of the cases this interval was ≤14 days. A comprehensive review of the scientific literature on soft tissue reconstruction after soft tissue sarcoma resection was conducted. Key prerequisites for maximum oncological safety and reconstructive reliability without delaying adjuvant therapy are plastic and reconstructive expertise within the sarcoma center, expedited pathological margin assessment and close collaboration with vascular surgery and radiotherapy.

title: Antiphospholipid syndrome: epidemiology and outcomes in the evolving criteria era.
abstract: Antiphospholipid syndrome (APS) is a heterogeneous autoimmune thrombo-inflammatory disorder characterized by thrombosis, pregnancy morbidity and an expanding spectrum of microvascular, cardiac, haematological and other systemic manifestations. Although research has provided considerable insights into the pathogenesis and clinical phenotypes of APS, its epidemiology remains difficult to define because estimates depend on case definitions, antibody testing, repeat-testing requirements, testing practices and data sources. Population-based studies suggest that APS is rare, and catastrophic APS is rarer and best understood through registry data. Antiphospholipid antibody positivity alone does not establish APS; transient or low-level positivity can occur without disease, whereas persistent antibodies must be interpreted alongside compatible clinical manifestations. Despite its rarity, APS causes substantial morbidity through recurrent thrombosis, organ damage and adverse pregnancy outcomes, supporting targeted evaluation in unprovoked or recurrent venous thromboembolism, stroke in younger adults and selected pregnancy complications. Apparent differences among populations can reflect ascertainment, access to testing, study design and biological variation. Standardized case definitions, antibody testing and laboratory reporting, together with longitudinal population-based research in ancestry-diverse, paediatric and low-income and middle-income populations, are needed to refine estimates of APS burden and define its clinical spectrum.

title: Clonal hematopoiesis is associated with adverse events in patients with high-grade carotid artery stenosis.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Clonal hematopoiesis (CH), defined as the expansion of a subset of hematopoietic stem or progenitor cells driven by acquired mutations, represents a novel cardiovascular risk factor. Its role in patients with high-grade carotid stenosis remains to be evaluated. PATIENTS AND METHODS: Next-generation sequencing (NGS) involving 30 genes implicated in CH was used as diagnostic-grade assay (SOPHiA DDM Myeloid Solution) to screen for CH in 83 prospectively collected patients with symptomatic or asymptomatic high-grade carotid stenosis undergoing carotid endarterectomy (CEA). RESULTS: P interaction Clonal markers were detected in 16 (19.7 %) of 83 patients (median age 71.2 years), with prevalence increasing at advanced age. At 5-year follow-up, CH carriers showed a higher cumulative incidence of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE; P = 0.040) compared to patients without CH; all-cause mortality did not differ significantly between groups (P = 0.57). Cox regression revealed a significant association between CH and MACE in a univariable model (P = 0.047), which remained significant after multivariable adjustment for age and sex (P = 0.018). Exploratory analyses suggested that the association between CH and MACE may differ according to carotid stenosis severity, with an increased incidence of MACE observed in patients with <90 % stenosis and concomitant CH, an effect absent in patients with ≥90 % stenosis ( = 0.03). DISCUSSION AND CONCLUSIONS: CH was associated with an adverse 5-year outcome in patients with carotid artery stenosis. These findings identify CH as a hematologic contributor to post-interventional cardiovascular risk and indicate that assessment of CH may offer additional prognostic information for residual risk stratification.

title: Cerebral metabolic rate of oxygen mapping on admission MRI may predict penumbral tissue fate in acute stroke patients treated successfully with thrombectomy.
abstract: PURPOSE: 2 Infarct growth occurs in most patients despite successful thrombectomy. We evaluated whether a dynamic susceptibility-contrast (DSC) perfusion-MRI surrogate of the cerebral metabolic rate of oxygen (CMRO) improves prediction of tissue fate within perfusion-diffusion mismatch regions after successful thrombectomy. METHODS: 2 2 In this retrospective analysis of the prospective HIBISCUS-STROKE registry, we included anterior-circulation stroke patients with admission DSC perfusion MRI, recanalization (mTICI ≥ 2b) after thrombectomy, and day-6T2-FLAIR MRI. Admission DSC-derived CMRO, cerebral blood flow (CBF), cerebral blood volume (CBV), and oxygen extraction fraction (OEF) were expressed as ratios to the mirrored contralateral region (rCMRO, rCBF, rCBV, rOEF) within mismatch subregions that infarcted (overlap with the day-6 lesion) or remained viable. All analyses accounted for within-patient clustering (generalized estimating equations, patient-level bootstrap and cross-validation). RESULTS: 2 2 2 Of 321 screened patients, 134 were included (median age, 71 years; 57.5 % men; median NIHSS score, 15), yielding 245 mismatch subregions (111 infarcted, 134 viable). rCMRO, rCBF, and rCBV were lower in infarcted than in viable subregions, whereas rOEF did not differ. rCMROprovided the best discrimination of infarction (AUC, 0.77; 95 % CI, 0.72-0.82), higher than rCBF (0.74; P = 0.04), rCBV (0.73; P = 0.001), and rOEF (0.52; P < 0.001); the gain over rCBF was modest (integrated discrimination improvement, 0.064; 95 % CI, 0.026-0.110). rCMRO<0.66 was selected in all cross-validation folds and independently predicted infarction (adjusted odds ratio, 8.02; 95 % CI, 4.60-14.01). CONCLUSIONS: 2 A DSC-MRI surrogate of CMROon admission discriminated infarct-destined from viable tissue within the perfusion-diffusion mismatch after successful thrombectomy, with a modest but consistent advantage over conventional perfusion metrics.

title: Rhodosporidium kratochvilovae RkMsn4, a zinc finger transcription factor, regulates carotenoid and lipid metabolism to enhance tolerance to environmental stress in.
abstract: Rhodosporidium kratochvilovae Rhodosporidium kratochvilovae Red yeasts serve as indispensable microbial resources for the production of carotenoids and lipids; however, environmental stress factors often limit their performance during industrial fermentation. The zinc-finger transcription factors Msn2/Msn4 act as central regulators of stress responses in yeasts. However, researchers have not yet systematically elucidated the similarities and differences in the mechanisms underlying the regulatory effects of Msn2/Msn4 under different stress conditions. In this study, we compared the shared and stress-specific regulatory functions of RkMsn4 inYM25235 under conditions of glucose starvation, 15 °C low temperature, and 4% NaCl salt stress. RkMsn4 contributed to the activity of the oxidative defense systems, including antioxidant enzymes, carotenoids, and glutathione, and the remodeling of membrane lipids, including phospholipids and unsaturated fatty acids (UFAs) across all three stress conditions. Additionally, RkMsn4 regulated stress-specific metabolic regulation by modulating branched-chain amino acid (BCAA) and aromatic amino acid (AAA) metabolism under glucose starvation conditions and promoting the utilization of exogenous sucrose and fructose under salt stress. By conducting weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA), we identified candidate genes potentially associated with carotenoid and lipid metabolism. These findings provide practical insights for improving tolerance to stress and metabolic productivity of red yeasts in industrial bioprocesses.IMPORTANCERed yeasts are important microorganisms for the production of carotenoids and lipids, but their performance is often limited by environmental stress. Understanding how red yeasts respond to environmental stress is crucial for advancing their application in industrial fermentation. This study reveals the stress response mechanisms mediated by the transcription factor RkMsn4 inYM25235 under glucose starvation, low temperature, and salt stress, as well as its regulatory role in carotenoid and lipid metabolism. These findings provide valuable insights for enhancing the stress resistance and productivity of red yeasts in industrial applications.

title: Physician-modified fenestrated thoracic endovascular aortic repair for a rapidly developing infectious distal aortic arch aneurysm after intravesical bacillus Calmette-Guérin therapy.
abstract: Mycobacterium tuberculosis An 84-year-old man developed hemoptysis 3 weeks after receiving intravesical bacillus Calmette-Guérin therapy for bladder cancer. Computed tomography revealed a new saccular distal aortic arch aneurysm involving the origin of the left subclavian artery, with periaortic inflammation. Computed tomography performed 3 months earlier had shown no aneurysm. Urine polymerase chain reaction testing was positive for thecomplex, supporting the diagnosis of a bacillus Calmette-Guérin-related infectious aortic aneurysm. Given the prohibitive surgical risk, emergency endovascular repair was performed using a physician-modified fenestrated endograft with branch revascularization in combination with antituberculous therapy. Hemoptysis resolved, and no recurrence was observed at 1-year follow-up.

abstract: We present a case of staged arch debranching with subsequent zone 0 branched thoracic aortic endograft in a patient with a bovine arch. This case highlights a staged hybrid endovascular and open approach to repairing a progressively aneurysmal aortic arch.

title: Rare common femoral vein adventitial cystic disease presenting with lower-extremity swelling.
abstract: Adventitial cystic disease (ACD) is a rare, nonatherosclerotic disorder caused by mucin-filled cysts within the vessel wall that produce luminal compression. Venous ACD is uncommon and may mimic deep vein thrombosis. A 24-year-old woman presented with right leg pain and swelling from a 2.8-cm common femoral vein cyst. The patient underwent cyst excision and bovine patch venoplasty but developed postoperative thrombosis from venoplasty-site stenosis and hematoma compression. Thrombectomy and angioplasty failed, requiring venous stenting. Pathology confirmed ACD. The patient recovered on enoxaparin and clopidogrel. This case emphasizes confirming durable venous outflow after cyst excision.

title: Unexpected para-aortic venous migration of n-butyl cyanoacrylate during transarterial sac embolization for a type II endoleak: A technical pitfall.
abstract: We report an unusual case of para-aortic venous migration of n-butyl cyanoacrylate (NBCA) during transarterial sac embolization for a type II endoleak after endovascular aneurysm repair. Preprocedural computed tomography and angiography demonstrated no venous communication. During progressive NBCA injection, sequential opacification of the fourth lumbar vein and a para-aortic venous structure became apparent, prompting immediate cessation of embolization. The patient remained asymptomatic, and follow-up imaging demonstrated stable aneurysm size without complications. This case highlights a rare technical pitfall and emphasizes careful fluoroscopic monitoring during NBCA sac embolization despite initially negative imaging findings.

title: High BMI-attributable burden of eight diseases relevant to the CKM framework in China: GBD 2023 estimates and projections to 2050.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome is a recently defined clinical entity integrating metabolic risk factors, chronic kidney disease, and cardiovascular disease. Elevated body mass index (BMI) is a major modifiable risk factor for CKM syndrome, yet comprehensive long-term analyses of the high BMI-attributable burden in China remain scarce. METHODS: Using data from the Global Burden of Disease (GBD) 2023 study, we assessed the burden of eight selected CKM-related diseases attributable to high BMI (atrial fibrillation and flutter [AFF], chronic kidney disease due to hypertension [CKD-HTN] or diabetes mellitus type 2 [CKD-T2DM], diabetes mellitus type 2 [T2DM], hypertensive heart disease [HHD], ischemic heart disease [IHD], lower extremity peripheral arterial disease [LEPAD], and stroke) in China from 1990 to 2023. The primary outcomes were absolute deaths and DALYs and their age-standardized rates (ASRs) per 100,000 population. Joinpoint regression and ARIMA models were applied to analyze and project temporal trends in ASRs, age-period-cohort analysis was conducted using age-specific rates, and decomposition analysis quantified the contributions of population growth, population aging, and epidemiological change to changes in absolute deaths and DALYs. RESULTS: From 1990 to 2023, absolute deaths and DALYs for all eight selected diseases relevant to the CKM framework increased. IHD had the highest burden in 2023 (114,980 deaths; 2,923,595 DALYs), whereas AFF showed the greatest relative increase (11.4-fold). Descriptively, men generally had higher point estimates of death and DALY counts, ASMRs, and ASDRs for CKD-T2DM, CKD-HTN, IHD, and HHD, whereas women had higher corresponding estimates for AFF. Joinpoint regression identified sustained increases in AFF, IHD, T2DM, and LEPAD, with several inflection points around 2005. APC analysis showed pronounced age-related gradients and variations in period and cohort rate ratios. Decomposition analysis indicated that population aging was the predominant contributor to increasing mortality for most outcomes, while epidemiological change had heterogeneous effects and partially offset increases in CKD-T2DM and HHD. Model-based projections suggested heterogeneous future trajectories: increasing mortality and DALY rates for AFF, IHD, and LEPAD; increasing DALYs but slightly declining mortality for T2DM; broadly stable or slightly declining rates for stroke, CKD-T2DM, and CKD-HTN; and declining point estimates for HHD, although with substantial long-term uncertainty. CONCLUSION: High BMI-attributable stage 2-4 CKM burden has risen sharply in China and will continue to increase, driven mainly by worsening epidemiological risks. AFF, IHD, and LEPAD show the fastest growth. Men had higher age-standardized mortality and DALY rates for several selected diseases. Early-life obesity prevention and sex-tailored interventions are urgently needed.

title: [Resection of locally advanced soft tissue sarcomas of the extremities : Surgical strategies to avoid postoperative complications].
abstract: Soft tissue sarcomas of the extremities are rare malignant tumors that constitute less than 1% of all malignant diseases. The aim of multimodal treatment is the complete surgical removal of the tumor into healthy tissue in the sense of an R0 resection. Due to the possible proximity to skin, blood vessels, nerves and bone, locally advanced sarcomas necessitate a specialized interdisciplinary treatment planning which leads to a complete resection of the sarcoma and also ensures a maximum preservation of function or limb. To achieve this, vascular surgical and plastic reconstructive interventions must be taken into consideration. Furthermore, postoperative complications, such as wound healing disorders, seromas and infections must be avoided in order not to delay the rehabilitation. This article summarizes the practice-oriented principles of the surgical treatment for locally advanced sarcomas of the extremities with a focus on the reduction of postoperative morbidity.

title: Methylene blue-guided parenchyma-sparing ex vivo resection and autotransplantation for a type III renal arteriovenous fistula with large renal vein aneurysm: A technical case report.
abstract: High-flow renal arteriovenous malformations (AVMs), type III with vein aneurysms, are rare and often require nephrectomy. A 54-year-old man presented with lumbar pain and hematuria. Computed tomography angiography revealed an 8- × 12-cm right renal vein aneurysm and a type III arteriovenous fistula occupying >30% of the kidney. After ex vivo nephrectomy with cold perfusion, selective methylene blue injection delineated the AVM nidus and parenchyma, guiding resection and excision. The procedure was performed by a multidisciplinary team including a vascular surgeon, transplant surgeon, and urologist. The kidney was reconstructed and reimplanted. Postoperative creatinine levels stabilized at 1.10 mg/dL, and computed tomography angiography confirmed AVM exclusion and preserved perfusion. Methylene blue mapping can enable parenchyma-sparing repair in selected cases.
